title: Core Rules: Radiance Patch Notes · Core Rules: Radiance Patch Notes (Effective October 16, 2026)
officialTextEn:
Read about the latest changes to core rules, along with some fun new interactions.
Announcements 2026-10-09T16:00:00.000Z
Radiance Rules Update Effective October 16, 2026
Welcome to the patch notes for Riftbound, Radiance edition. Included in today’s update are rules for playing with Radiance’s new mechanics, updates from the Vendetta FAQ , improvements to the rules’ logical infrastructure to better prepare for future sets and mechanics and a collection of scenarios to help folks understand some of the more complicated interactions introduced with Radiance .

title: Core Rules: Radiance Patch Notes · Unique Radiance Interactions
officialTextEn:
While the patch notes and core rules are aimed at arming our judges, we wanted to include questions and answers prepared by the design team for some of the more tricky interactions and cards released in that set. This article will be released in addition to an FAQ article in the window when we’ve previously released FAQ articles.
Although this article is not an FAQ, it still is a collection of official rulings. These rulings are based on the Core Rules Document that also releases today, as well as the wording of the cards. When a new version of the Core Rules Document is released, it will take precedence over any points that differ from this document.
Throughout this document, we use some specific shorthand to represent symbols in card text. Here’s a short guide:
[E] means “exhaust”
[M] means “Might”
[A] means “one power of any domain”
[C] means “one power of this card’s domain” [C] in Accelerate costs takes on the domain of the Unit, or turns into [A] if the Unit has no domain or multiple domains.
[C] in other cases is treated as the corresponding power symbol in all respects, matching how the cards are actually printed—it’s just a design shorthand!
What happens when I play Ekko, Boy Who Shattered Time’s activated ability, play a unit, and then play Unlicensed Armoy’s activated ability? Will the unit be killed on my next turn?
Your unit’s death from its triggered ability will be replaced by Unlicensed Armory. Although the unit has the text “Kill me at end of turn.” appended to it, that text is synonymous with “Kill me at the end of this turn.” On subsequent turns, it will not trigger.
When “at end of turn” appears on card text, it is used synonymously with “at the end of this turn.” Although granting that text to a unit is strange, it isn’t outside the bounds of possibility. If the unit remains on the board after the triggered ability resolves, the condition for its ability to trigger will no longer be able to be fulfilled, so it will not trigger again. If the unit changes zones to or from a non-board zone prior to the triggered ability triggering, all of its temporary modifications—including this granted text—will be removed. As such, the ability will no longer exist to trigger.
Relevant rules: 359.3.e.16., 124.1.
Can I show off a facedown card at a battlefield with the Show Off ability of Gutter Guardian?
You cannot. Facedown cards don’t have any referenceable characteristics from their front side.
The keyword “Hidden” only appears on the front side of the card; that’s the side with the cost, name, Might, and rules text among other traits. While a card is facedown, any information on its front side cannot be referenced by other cards and effects. Although a facedown card may be friendly to Gutter Guardian, it doesn’t have the appropriate characteristic to be shown off. Note that only the card from hand is revealed with Show Off. You don’t reveal the friendly objects on the board that you’re Showing Off, so you can’t reveal the facedown card even if you wanted to.
Relevant rules: 811.5.a., 129.4.
What’s up with the reminder text on Chronobreak? Do I get to choose the order?
You get to choose the order if you own all of the units being banished. If you control some number of units that you don’t own and banish those units as well, the units you banish will be placed on the chain starting with units owned by the current turn player and then proceeding in turn order.
Items cannot be placed on the chain simultaneously for any reason. If chain items would be played simultaneously, their controller chooses the order they go on the chain. If multiple players would add items to the chain simultaneously, they place their items on the chain in turn order instead, starting with the current turn player. In the case of Chronobreak, each player chooses the order of their own units being played to the chain (this is what the reminder text is referring to), but each player plays their units to the chain in turn order, starting with the current turn player.
officialTextKo:
패치 노트와 핵심 규칙은 심판 여러분께 정보를 제공하기 위한 것이지만, 이번 세트에서 출시된 카드와 까다로운 상호작용에 관해 기획 팀이 준비한 질의응답을 함께 수록했습니다. 이전에 FAQ를 공개했던 시기에 이 문서와 FAQ 문서를 함께 공개할 예정입니다.
이 문서는 FAQ가 아니지만, 공식 판정을 모아놓은 문서입니다. 이러한 판정은 오늘 함께 공개되는 핵심 규칙 문서와 카드의 설명을 기반으로 합니다. 새로운 버전의 핵심 규칙 문서가 공개되면, 이 문서와 상충하는 모든 내용에 대해 새로운 핵심 규칙이 우선적으로 적용됩니다.
이 문서에서는 카드 텍스트의 기호를 나타내기 위해 몇 가지 특정 약어를 이용합니다. 간단히 설명해 드리자면 다음과 같습니다.
[E]는 '탈진'을 의미합니다.
[M]은 '위력'을 의미합니다.
[A]는 '아무 영역의 힘 1'을 의미합니다.
[C]는 '이 카드 영역의 힘 1'을 의미합니다. 가속 비용에서 [C]는 해당 유닛의 영역을 따르며, 영역이 없거나 다수의 영역에 속할 경우 [A]로 취급됩니다.
그 외의 경우 [C]는 카드에 실제로 인쇄된 해당 힘 기호와 모든 측면에서 완전히 동일하게 취급됩니다. 이는 디자인 편의를 위한 축약입니다!
'에코, 시간을 달리는 소년'의 발동 스킬을 사용하고 유닛을 사용한 다음, 무허가 무기고의 발동 스킬을 사용하면 어떻게 되나요? 다음 제 턴에 유닛이 처치되나요?
'에코, 시간을 달리는 소년'의 유발 스킬로 인해 내 유닛이 사망하는 효과가 무허가 무기고로 대체됩니다. '에코, 시간을 달리는 소년'에 '턴 종료 시 이 카드를 처치합니다.'라는 문구가 있지만, 해당 문구는 '이번 턴 종료 시 이 카드 처치'와 동일한 의미입니다. 따라서, 이후 턴에서는 유발되지 않습니다.
카드 텍스트에 '턴 종료 시'라고 표시된 효과는 '이번 턴 종료 시'와 같은 의미로 사용됩니다. 유닛에게 해당 효과를 부여하는 것이 이상하긴 하지만, 불가능한 것은 아닙니다. 유발 스킬이 처리된 후에도 유닛이 게임판에 남아 있다면, 해당 스킬의 유발 조건이 더 이상 충족될 수 없으므로 스킬이 다시 유발되지 않습니다. 유발 스킬이 유발되기 전에 유닛이 게임판 외 구역으로 또는 그곳에서 다른 구역으로 이동하면, 부여된 이 텍스트를 비롯하여 이 유닛에 적용된 모든 일시적 변경 사항이 제거됩니다. 따라서 스킬이 유발되지 않습니다.
관련 규칙: 359.3.e.16, 124.1
뒷골목 수호자의 과시 스킬로 전장에 있는 뒷면 표시 카드를 과시할 수 있나요?
과시할 수 없습니다. 뒷면 표시 카드는 앞면의 어떠한 특징도 지칭할 수 없기 때문입니다.
'숨겨짐' 키워드는 카드의 앞면에만 표시됩니다. 카드 앞면에는 비용, 이름, 위력, 규칙 텍스트 등의 특성이 표시되는데, 카드가 뒷면 표시 상태인 동안에는 다른 카드나 효과가 카드 앞면의 어떤 정보도 지칭할 수 없습니다. 뒷면 표시 카드가 뒷골목 수호자의 아군일 수도 있지만, 과시할 특징은 가지고 있지 않습니다. 과시로는 손에 있는 카드만 공개된다는 점에 유의하세요. 과시하기로 선택한 게임판의 아군 오브젝트는 공개되지 않으므로, 원하더라도 뒷면 표시 카드를 공개할 수 없습니다.
관련 규칙: 811.5.a, 129.4
'시공간 붕괴'의 참고 텍스트는 어떻게 된 건가요? 제가 순서를 정할 수 있나요?
추방할 모든 유닛을 보유하고 있다면 순서를 정할 수 있습니다. 자신이 소유하지 않은 유닛을 일정 수 통제하고 있는 상태에서 해당 유닛들까지 추방할 경우, 추방된 유닛들은 현재 턴 플레이어가 소유한 유닛부터 시작하여 턴 순서대로 체인에 놓입니다.
어떠한 경우에도 여러 항목을 동시에 체인에 놓을 수는 없습니다. 체인 항목이 동시에 사용될 경우에는 해당 항목의 통제자가 체인에 놓일 순서를 정합니다. 여러 플레이어가 동시에 항목을 체인에 놓을 경우, 현재 턴 플레이어부터 시작하여 턴 순서에 따라 자신의 항목을 체인에 놓습니다. 시공간 붕괴의 경우, 각 플레이어는 체인에 사용할 자신의 유닛 순서를 정하지만(참고 텍스트가 언급하는 내용), 각 플레이어는 현재 턴 플레이어부터 시작하여 턴 순서에 따라 자신의 유닛을 체인에 사용합니다.
예시: 총 5개의 유닛을 통제하고 있으며, 그중 둘은 상대의 소유입니다. 시공간 붕괴를 사용하여 유닛 다섯을 모두 선택합니다. 모든 유닛을 추방한 후, 각 유닛의 소유자가 해당 유닛을 미확정 항목으로 체인에 사용합니다. 내가 현재 턴 플레이어이므로 원하는 순서대로 유닛 셋을 먼저 사용한 다음, 상대가 원하는 순서대로 유닛 둘을 사용합니다. 미확정 체인 항목은 오래된 것부터 순서대로 확정되며, 유닛은 확정되는 즉시 처리됩니다. 따라서 내가 체인에 사용한 첫 번째 유닛부터 시작하여 체인에 더 이상 유닛이 남지 않을 때까지 미확정 유닛을 모두 확정하고 처리합니다. 그 후, 유발 순서에 따라 해당 유닛들의 사용 효과를 확정합니다. 마지막으로, 플레이어들은 체인의 가장 최근 항목에 대해 반응을 이용할 수 있습니다. 반응하지 않으면 해당 항목은 처리되고, 이후 체인에 있는 모든 항목이 처리될 때까지 이 과정을 반복합니다.
관련 규칙: 303.2.a
치환술사의 발동 스킬을 사용해 강화 상태인 6 [M]의 '갱플랭크, 바다의 지배자'를 선택하면 어떻게 되나요? 아귀 용을 사용할 수 있나요?
갱플랭크가 손으로 되돌아가는 효과가 이번 턴에 +3 [M]을 획득하는 효과로 대체됩니다. 그러므로, 치환술사의 발동 스킬로 손에서 아귀 용을 사용할 수 있습니다.
치환술사는 유닛 하나를 손으로 돌려보낸 후 해당 유닛의 정보를 지칭합니다. 유닛이 구역을 벗어나지 않았고 해당 유닛을 대상으로 지정한 지시가 처리되는 과정에서 유효한 대상이었다면, 유발 스킬은 해당 유닛의 현재 정보를 지칭합니다. '갱플랭크, 바다의 지배자'의 현재 위력은 지칭된 대로 9 [M]이므로, 비용이 9 [M] 이하인 유닛을 사용할 수 있습니다.
관련 규칙: 359.3.e.13, 359.3.e.13.a
'오리아나, 시계태엽 소녀'로 부착된 장비를 선택하면 어떻게 되나요?
장비가 유닛이 되면 부착된 오브젝트에서 분리됩니다. 장착 스킬을 발동할 수 있고 무기의 대가 유발 효과의 대상으로 지정될 수 있지만, 유닛에 부착될 수는 없습니다. 따라서 해당 스킬이 처리될 때 아무 일도 일어나지 않습니다.
이번 규칙 업데이트에서는 유닛을 다른 게임 오브젝트에 부착할 수 없다는 점을 명확히 했습니다. 유닛을 게임 오브젝트에 부착해야 한다면, 먼저 유닛 상태를 해제해야 합니다. 비유닛 게임 오브젝트가 유닛이 되면, 유닛이 되었으므로 부착된 대상에서 분리됩니다. 어떤 효과가 유닛 상태를 해제하지 않고 유닛을 다른 게임 오브젝트에 부착하려고 하면, 아무 일도 일어나지 않습니다.
관련 규칙: 143.5, 435.1.h, 718.6
'오리아나, 시계태엽 소녀'로 전장에 있는 배치 도구를 선택하면 어떻게 되나요?
해당 도구는 유발 스킬이 처리될 때 유닛 도구가 됩니다. 도구의 통제자가 해당 전장을 통제하지 않은 경우 해당 전장에 경합 상태를 적용하며, 이후 정리 단계에서 전투 또는 결전이 실행 대기 상태가 됩니다. 체인이 정리되면 해당 결전 또는 전투가 시작됩니다.
관련 규칙: 190.3.a, 323.7, 323.8, 323.11, 323.12
'오리아나, 시계태엽 소녀'로 다른 도구를 선택하여 이전 유닛 도구의 유닛 상태가 해제되면 어떻게 되나요? 해당 도구에 부착된 장비는 분리되나요? 기지에 있는 배치 도구라면 이동시킬 수 있나요?
부착된 장비는 부착 상태가 유지되며, 기지에 있는 배치 도구일 경우 기지에 남습니다.
유닛은 오브젝트에 부착될 수 없지만, 다른 오브젝트는 아무런 제약 없이 부착될 수 있습니다. 유닛이 되지 않은 부착된 장비는 도구의 유닛 상태가 해제된 후에도 계속 부착되어 있습니다. 도구에는 위력이 없으므로 장비의 추가 위력은 적용되지 않지만, 효과 텍스트는 부착된 도구에 계속 적용됩니다.
대부분의 배치 도구에는 '이 전장' 또는 '이곳을 점거'와 같은 문구가 있으므로 기지에서는 효과를 얻을 수 없습니다. 그렇긴 하지만, '오리아나, 시계태엽 소녀'로 다시 유닛으로 만들거나 명령: 공격과 같이 도구 이동을 지정하는 이동 효과를 사용하면 해당 도구를 전장으로 다시 이동시킬 수 있습니다.

title: Core Rules: Radiance Patch Notes · Unique Radiance Interactions (2)
officialTextEn:
Example: You control five total units, two of which are owned by your opponent. You play Chronobreak, choosing all five units. You banish them, then for each, their owner plays them to the chain as pending items. You’re the current turn player, so you play your three units first in the order of your choice, then your opponent plays their two units in the order of their choice. Pending chain items are finalized from oldest to newest and units resolve as soon as they’re finalized. Thus, we go up the chain starting with the first unit you played to the chain, finalizing and resolving all of the pending units on the chain until there are no more units on the chain. Then we finalize any play effects of those units in the order they triggered. Finally, players can react to the most recent item on the chain. If they don’t, that item resolves, and we repeat the process until all items on the chain have resolved.
Relevant rules: 303.2.a.
What happens when I play Transpositionist’s activated ability choosing an empowered Gangplank, Naval with 6 [M]? Can I play Angler Wyrm?
Gangplank being returned to hand will be replaced with him being given +3 [M] this turn. You can play Angler Wyrm from hand with Transpositionist’s activated ability.
Transpositionist returns a unit to hand and then references that unit’s information. If the unit didn’t change zones and it was a legal target as the instruction that targeted it was being processed, the activated ability will reference that unit’s current information. Gangplank, Naval’s current Might as it is referenced is 9 [M], allowing you to play a unit with 9 [M] or less.
Relevant rules: 359.3.e.13., 359.3.e.13.a.
What happens when I choose an attached Equipment with Orianna, Lady of Clockwork?
It detaches from the object it is attached to when it becomes a unit. Although its equip ability can be activated and it can be targeted by Weaponmaster triggers, it cannot attach to a unit; nothing will happen when those abilities resolve.
In this rules update we’ve clarified that units cannot be attached to other game objects. If a unit were to be attached to a game object, it would need to stop being a unit first. If a non-unit game object becomes a unit, it will detach from anything it is attached to as it becomes a unit. If an effect would attempt to attach a unit to another game object without making it no longer a unit first, nothing happens.
Relevant rules: 143.5., 435.1.h., 718.6.
What happens when I choose a gear with Deploy located at a battlefield with Orianna, Lady of Clockwork?
That gear will become a unit-gear when the triggered ability resolves; if their controller doesn’t control that battlefield, they will apply contested status to that battlefield, and a combat or showdown will be staged there in the subsequent cleanup. When the chain clears, that showdown or combat will open.
Relevant rules: 190.3.a., 323.7, 323.8., 323.11., 323.12.
What happens when I choose another gear with Orianna, Lady of Clockwork and the previous unit-gear stops being a unit? Will its attached Equipment fall off? If it’s a deploy gear in base, do I get to move it?
Its attached Equipment will remain attached, and if it is a Deploy gear in base, it will remain in base.
Although units cannot be attached to objects, other objects have no such compunctions. Any attached Equipment that don’t become units will remain attached to the gear even after it stops being a unit. Their Might bonus won’t apply, since the gear doesn’t have a Might, but they will continue to apply their effect text to the gear they are attached to.
The majority of gear with Deploy reference “this battlefield” or “hold here” in such a way that gaining a benefit from base is not possible. That being said, if you want to move it back to a battlefield you can either turn it into a unit again with Orianna, Lady of Clockwork or you can use movement effects that specify moving gear, such as Command: Attack.

title: Core Rules: Radiance Patch Notes · Unique Radiance Interactions (3)
officialTextEn:
Note that there is a small gap between finalizing the Orianna, Lady of Clockwork trigger causing the previous unit-gear to stop being a unit, and the triggered ability resolving and causing the new gear to become a unit. During that gap, neither gear is a unit unless it was already one prior to ever being chosen by Orianna, Lady of Clockwork.
Relevant rules: 137.3.b.
So how does Neeko, Blending In actually work? When do I choose the legends, do I get three legends per Neeko in my deck, can I add multiple of the same legend to the Legend Zone, do the legends enter ready, and do I need to reveal them to my opponent?
You choose the legends during deck building—at competitive OPL, you must register those legends as part of your deck list, and you can store them with your sideboard. The 3 legends are shared by all Neekos in your deck. You cannot add multiple of the same legend to the Legend Zone. The legends enter ready. You do not need to reveal them to your opponent until they are added to the Legend Zone.
Let’s break down Neeko’s rules text. If your deck (Main Deck or sideboard) has one or more copies of Neeko, Blending In, you pick three legends in addition to your starting Champion Legend. Those 3 legends must be different from each other and from your Champion Legend. Regardless of how many copies of Neeko you have in your deck, you will choose three legends in this way.
When Neeko’s play effect resolves, its controller picks one of the legends chosen during deck building and adds it to their Legend Zone alongside their Champion Legend for as long as Neeko is on the board. If Neeko leaves the board, that legend will also cease to exist. The legends don’t exist in any zone of the game while they’re not in the Legend Zone; they don’t exist at all. That being said, if one or more of those legends are already on the board, a player can’t choose to create additional versions of those legends; they can have at most one legend on the board per legend chosen during deckbuilding. If somehow a player played a fourth Neeko, they would fail to add a legend to their legend zone.
The legends added this way are not tokens. They are legend cards and behave in all ways like normal legends do. If an effect instructs a player to “ready a friendly legend” they can target and ready any legends controlled by them or an ally. If an effect instructs a player to ready “your legend,” that refers to any legend controlled by that player. Such an effect does not target a legend; the legend is chosen as the spell or ability resolves.
Relevant rules: 103.1., 440.2.a., 440.3.b., 440.3.c., 355.10.g.
What happens when the unit on the board that I Showed Off with Primordial Roar is returned to my hand with Star-Crossed? Do I still deal damage? What about if I play Lunar Boon and discard the unit from hand?
You still deal damage in both scenarios.
Any referenced characteristics of shown off objects are locked in when you show them off. Regardless of what subsequently happens to them, their information will be able to be checked by the card that showed them off. This also means that giving a unit +[M] or -[M] after showing that unit off will not affect the damage dealt by Primordial Roar; it’s too late by that point.
Relevant rules: 832.1.d.1.
What counts as reducing a unit’s Might for Ahri, Confident? If I play Discipline on my 1 [M] unit while it’s stunned and located at the same battlefield as an enemy Leona, Zealot, will I trigger their Ahri, Confident located at that battlefield?
Reducing a unit’s Might means an ability of an object you control causes a unit to receive a -[M] effect. Ahri, Confident will trigger if you Discipline a stunned 1 [M] unit at the same battlefield as an enemy Leona, Zealot.

title: Core Rules: Radiance Patch Notes · Unique Radiance Interactions (4)
officialTextEn: Although Discipline never causes the unit’s Might to increase, the unit goes from 1 [M] with a -0 [M] effect applied to it, which will not trigger Ahri, Confident, to 3 [M] with a -2 [M] effect applied to it. This change in state triggers Ahri, Confident, the same as a 3 [M] unit being stunned and receiving a -2 [M] effect from Leona, Zealot’s passive ability. Note that this doesn’t work for other cases: if a stunned 3 [M] unit at the same battlefield as an enemy Leona, Zealot has Discipline played on it, that unit will not have a new Might reduction effect applied to it and thus Ahri, Confident will not trigger. Spells, triggered abilities, and activated abilities are easier; if a spell, triggered ability, or activated ability applies non-zero -[M] to a unit, Ahri, Confident will trigger.

title: Core Rules: Radiance Patch Notes · Core Rules Changes
officialTextEn:
The Unleashed and Vendetta rules updates have laid a relatively stable base for this rules update. We’ve made small changes as necessary, but we have fewer logical holes to patch, and there aren’t any sweeping fixes that need to be implemented in this set. The vast majority of the rules in this update are about new cards and mechanics in the Radiance set.
Now let’s take a look at the rules changes we have in store for Radiance !
—
Radiance Addition: Deploy
Deploy is a new keyword appearing on gear in Radiance. Gear with Deploy enable players to apply localized, battlefield-altering effects.
Gear with Deploy can be played to any battlefield; enemy occupied, friendly, or uncontrolled. However, when an opponent holds a battlefield where you have gear with Deploy, those gear will be killed.
Gear with Deploy remain at their current battlefield so long as they aren’t destroyed. Some effects can move gear with Deploy to other battlefields too! NEW RULE: Deploy keyword added.
Radiance Addition: Disarm
Disarm is a new keyword appearing on units in Radiance.
Disarm is an attack trigger. The first time a unit with Disarm attacks each combat, they will give an enemy unit at their battlefield -1 [M] this turn. If a unit has Disarm 2, they’ll give an enemy unit -2 [M] this turn.
Disarm stacks just like Assault or Shield; meaning if a unit has gained multiple Disarm keywords from different sources, the unit will have one trigger for Disarm with a total of the sum of their Disarm values. NEW RULE: Disarm keyword added.
Radiance Addition: Show Off
Show Off is a new keyword appearing on both units and spells in Radiance.
When you Show Off something, you reveal a card from your hand that matches the requirement, or pick a friendly game object (card or token) on the board with the appropriate characteristics.
Cards with Show Off can reference information from the shown off card or object. That information is locked in when the card or object is shown off, even if it’s referenced later. NEW RULE: Show Off keyword added.
Rules Update: Copy Effects Layer
We saw some confusion on how copy effects work and their placement in the trait-altering layer. In the Radiance rules update, we’ve moved to clarify this by giving copy effects a layer of their own. The first layer is now for copy effects and all subsequent layers (trait-altering, ability-altering, arithmetic) have been shifted down to reflect this change.
Because copy effects only interacted with other copy effects anyway, there was functionally no reason for them to remain in the trait-altering layer. Our hope with this move is that it will be clearer that they only interact with other copy effects. Effects like the Mech tag appended by Experimental Hexplate in the trait-altering layer are not copied by copy effects. NEW RULE: Copy Effects layer added.
Radiance Addition: Copy Game Action
To support and build on this clarification for copy effects, we’ve also added the copy game action to the game actions section.
This section also clarifies how game objects that are created as copies, like the tokens played by Zilean, Time Mage’s replacement effect, work; those game objects don’t have a copy effect applied to them, but are created directly with the copyable traits of the object it is a copy of, as if those were its own printed traits. NEW RULE: Copy game action added.
Radiance Support: Additional Deckbuilding Decisions
Radiance ’s Neeko, Blending In adds the first instance of additional choices made during deckbuilding, so we’ve added rules to clarify how those choices are made. NEW RULE: Additional deckbuilding decisions added.
Radiance Support: Equipment Units
Orianna, Lady of Clockwork presents some unique rules scenarios for the game, including what happens to an Equipment that becomes a unit. We decided on the simplest answer: units can’t be attached to other game objects. If an attached game object becomes a unit, it detaches immediately. CLARIFIED RULE: Units cannot be attached to other game objects.
CLARIFIED RULE: If an attached non-unit game object becomes a unit, it detaches as it becomes a unit.
Rules Update: Layer Calculations and Object Dependencies
officialTextKo:
언리시드 와 벤데타 규칙 업데이트로 이번 규칙 업데이트에는 비교적 안정적인 기반이 마련되었습니다. 이에 따라 필요한 부분만 소규모로 변경했으며, 메워야 할 논리적 허점도 줄어들어 이번 세트에 전면적인 대규모 수정 사항은 없습니다. 이번 업데이트에 포함된 규칙 대부분은 레디언스 세트의 신규 카드 및 체계에 관한 내용입니다.
이제 레디언스 에 적용될 규칙 변경 사항을 살펴보겠습니다!
—
레디언스 추가 사항: 배치
배치는 레디언스 의 도구에 등장하는 신규 키워드입니다. 배치 도구를 통해 플레이어는 국지적으로 전장을 변화시키는 효과를 적용할 수 있습니다.
배치 도구는 적이 점령한 전장, 아군 전장, 미통제 전장 등 아무 전장에 사용할 수 있습니다. 하지만 상대가 내 배치 도구가 있는 전장을 점거하면 해당 도구는 처치됩니다.
배치 도구는 파괴되지 않는 한 현재 전장에 계속 남습니다. 일부 효과를 통해 배치 도구를 다른 전장으로 이동시킬 수도 있습니다! 새로운 규칙: 배치 키워드가 추가되었습니다.
레디언스 추가 사항: 무장 해제
무장 해제는 레디언스 의 유닛에 등장하는 신규 키워드입니다.
무장 해제는 공격 유발 효과입니다. 무장 해제 유닛이 전투마다 처음으로 공격하면, 이번 턴에 해당 전장에 있는 적 유닛 1명에게 -1 [M]을 부여합니다. 유닛이 무장 해제 2를 가지고 있을 경우, 이번 턴에 적 유닛 1명에게 -2 [M]을 부여합니다.
무장 해제는 맹공이나 보호막처럼 중첩됩니다. 즉, 유닛이 서로 다른 요소로부터 무장 해제 키워드를 여러 개 얻은 경우, 해당 유닛은 각 무장 해제 수치를 총합한 단일 무장 해제 유발 효과를 가집니다. 새로운 규칙: 무장 해제 키워드가 추가되었습니다.
레디언스 추가 사항: 과시
과시는 레디언스 의 유닛 및 주문에 등장하는 신규 키워드입니다.
무언가를 과시하면, 손에서 요구 사항에 맞는 카드 1장을 공개하거나, 게임판에 있는 적절한 특징을 가진 아군 게임 오브젝트(카드 또는 토큰) 1개를 고릅니다.
과시 카드는 과시한 카드 또는 오브젝트의 정보를 지칭할 수 있습니다. 해당 정보는 카드 또는 오브젝트를 과시할 때 고정되며, 이후 다시 지칭되더라도 변경되지 않습니다. 새로운 규칙: 과시 키워드가 추가되었습니다.
규칙 업데이트: 복사 효과 레이어
복사 효과의 작동 방식 및 특성 변경 레이어 내 위치에 대한 약간의 혼동을 확인했습니다. 이번 레디언스 규칙 업데이트에서는 복사 효과 전용 레이어를 새로 부여해 이 부분을 명확히 했습니다. 이제 첫 번째 레이어에 복사 효과가 배정되며, 이 변경 사항을 반영하여 이후의 모든 레이어(특성 변경, 스킬 변경, 연산)는 한 단계씩 뒤로 밀려납니다.
복사 효과는 다른 복사 효과와만 상호작용하므로, 기능적으로 특성 변경 레이어에 남아 있을 이유가 없었습니다. 이번 변경 사항을 통해 복사 효과가 오직 다른 복사 효과와만 상호작용한다는 사실이 더욱 명확해지기를 바랍니다. 예를 들어, 특성 변경 레이어에서 실험적 마공학판에 의해 추가된 메크 태그 같은 효과는 복사 효과로 복사되지 않습니다. 새로운 규칙: 복사 효과 레이어가 추가되었습니다.
레디언스 추가 사항: 복사 게임 행동
복사 효과에 대한 이번 명확화 내용을 보완하고자, 게임 행동 조항에 복사 게임 행동을 추가했습니다.
또한 이 조항은 '질리언, 시간의 마법사' 대체 효과에 의해 사용되는 토큰 등 복사본으로 생성되는 게임 오브젝트의 작동 방식을 명확히 설명합니다. 이러한 게임 오브젝트는 복사 효과가 적용되는 것이 아닌, 마치 카드 자체에 고유 특성이 인쇄된 것처럼 복사 대상 오브젝트의 복사 가능한 특성을 지닌 채 생성됩니다. 새로운 규칙: 복사 게임 행동이 추가되었습니다.
레디언스 지원 사항: 추가 덱 구성 결정
레디언스 의 '니코, 동화'는 덱 구성 과정에서 추가적인 선택을 하도록 하는 첫 번째 사례인 만큼, 이러한 선택이 어떻게 이루어지는지 명확히 설명하는 규칙을 추가했습니다. 새로운 규칙: 추가 덱 구성 결정이 추가되었습니다.
레디언스 지원 사항: 장비 유닛
'오리아나, 시계태엽 소녀'는 유닛이 된 장비에 일어나는 일을 포함해 게임 내 몇 가지 독특한 규칙 상황을 만들어냅니다. 개발 팀은 가장 명확하고 간단한 해답을 선택했습니다. 유닛은 다른 게임 오브젝트에 부착될 수 없다는 것입니다. 부착된 게임 오브젝트가 유닛이 되면, 해당 오브젝트는 즉시 분리됩니다. 규칙 명확화: 유닛은 다른 게임 오브젝트에 부착할 수 없습니다.
규칙 명확화: 부착된 비유닛 게임 오브젝트가 유닛이 될 경우, 유닛이 될 때 분리됩니다.
규칙 업데이트: 레이어 계산 및 오브젝트 종속성
향후 상호작용을 지원하고 레이어 효과 계산 방식을 명확히 하고자 레이어 계산 규칙을 추가했습니다.
레이어 효과를 계산할 때, 각 게임 오브젝트는 개별적으로 취급됩니다. 한 게임 오브젝트가 다른 게임 오브젝트의 정보를 지칭해야 할 경우, 게임은 해당 게임 오브젝트의 레이어 정보를 먼저 평가한 후 다시 돌아와 원래 게임 오브젝트의 정보를 계산합니다.
여러 게임 오브젝트가 서로의 정보를 지칭하는 경우, 대신 레이어별로 모든 오브젝트의 정보를 동시에 평가합니다. 새로운 규칙: 레이어 계산 절차가 추가되었습니다.
규칙 업데이트: 고르기
'고르기'는 카드에 새롭게 등장하기 시작한 단어이며, 이는 내년 초 레거시 출시와 함께 더 중요해질 예정입니다. 고르기는 앞으로 대상 지정이 아닌 선택을 내리는 상황에 사용하고자 하는 단어입니다. 카드가 무언가를 '선택'하라고 지시한다면, 이는 선택 대상을 지정하는 것임을 플레이어 여러분이 명확하게 인지하기를 바랍니다.
향후 레거시 규칙 및 템플릿 변경 사항이 카드 텍스트에 적용되면, 현재 '선택'이라고 적혀 있는 다수의 카드 텍스트가 '고르기'로 업데이트됩니다. 레디언스 에서도 이러한 작업이 일부 진행됩니다. 이에 따라 레거시 규칙 업데이트에 앞서 규칙 문서에서 이 부분을 명확하게 정리하고자 합니다. 새로운 규칙: 고르기가 추가되었습니다.
규칙 업데이트: 조건부 구절 범위
벤데타 에서는 지시 텍스트 내 조건부 구절 범위에 대해 일부 플레이어 여러분이 혼란을 느낄 만한 상황이 있었습니다.
레디언스 규칙 업데이트에서는 지시 내에서 조건부 구절이 어느 범위까지 적용되는지를 명확히 했습니다. 새로운 규칙: 조건부 구절 범위가 추가되었습니다.
규칙 업데이트: 확정 시점 행동 범위
비용 지불 또는 행동 수행 여부를 확인하는 카드의 'you' 표기가, 다른 플레이어가 해당 카드의 통제를 획득했을 때 혼란을 유발한다는 피드백을 받았습니다. 이 부분을 명확히 하는 새로운 규칙을 추가했습니다. 새로운 규칙: 주문 또는 스킬의 지시는 확정 단계에서 수행된 행동을 지칭할 수 있습니다. 이는 '내가' 해당 게임 행동을 수행했는지 확인하는 방식으로 작동합니다.
새로운 규칙: 이러한 지시는 해당 게임 행동 수행 여부만을 확인하며, 누가 수행했는지는 확인하지 않습니다. 확정 단계에서 게임 행동이 수행된 후 다른 플레이어가 해당 주문 또는 스킬의 통제를 획득하더라도, 이 지시에서는 여전히 조건을 충족한 것으로 간주합니다.
규칙 업데이트: 선택 다시하기
벤데타 규칙 업데이트에서는 신비한 전환 및 반박 등의 카드에 이용되는 선택 다시하기 모델을 추가한 바 있습니다. 이 규칙이 불분명하다는 피드백을 받았고, 벤데타 FAQ를 통해 임시 모델 작동 방식을 안내해 드렸습니다. 이후 재검토 결과 이 조치가 그다지 만족스럽지 않다는 결론을 내렸고, 새로운 결정을 내리는 방식을 더 간단하고 직관적으로 개편하기로 했습니다.
이제 새로운 결정을 내릴 때는, 처음부터 다시 모든 결정을 새롭게 내려야 합니다. 이전과 동일한 결정을 선택할 수도 있지만, 새로운 결정을 내리기로 했다면 일부만 바꿀 수는 없습니다.
이전 모델과 마찬가지로 모든 결정은 적합하고 유효해야 합니다. 다만, 이번 새 모델에서는, 예를 들어 대상 지정 시 유발되는 스킬의 경우, 이전에 동일한 유닛을 대상으로 지정했더라도 다시 유발됩니다. 즉, 대상 선택 절차를 완전히 처음부터 다시 거치는 느낌에 가깝습니다. 규칙 명확화: 선택 다시하기가 업데이트되었습니다.
규칙 업데이트: 미확정 항목 대상 적합성

title: Core Rules: Radiance Patch Notes · Core Rules Changes (2)
officialTextEn:
We’ve added rules for layer calculations in an effort to support future interactions and clarify how the layer effects are calculated.
When calculating layer effects, each game object is treated individually. If a game object needs to reference information from another game object, the game evaluates that game object’s layer information before returning to calculate the original game object’s information.
If multiple game objects reference information from each other, instead evaluate all of their information simultaneously, layer by layer. NEW RULE: Layer calculation procedure added.
Rules Update: Pick
We’re starting to see the word “pick” appear on cards, which will become even more important when Legacy releases early next year. Pick is the word we’re moving towards for when you make a choice that isn’t a target. We want to make it clear to players that when a card says for you to “choose” something, that means you are targeting what you choose.
When the Legacy rules and templating change is implemented in card text, many cards that currently say “choose” will have their text updated to pick. We are doing some of that work in Radiance. As such, we can also make this clearer in the rules prior to the Legacy rules update. NEW RULE: Pick added.
Rules Update: Conditional Clause Scope
In Vendetta we saw some players understandably confused over the scope of conditional clauses in instruction text.
With the Radiance rules update, we’ve clarified what scope conditional clauses have in a given instruction. NEW RULE: Conditional clauses scope added.
Rules Update: Finalizing Time Actions Scope
We received feedback that cards which referred to “you” when checking if costs were paid or actions were taken was confusing if control of the card is gained by another player. New rules have been added to clarify this. NEW RULE: Instructions of a spell or ability may reference actions taken during Finalization. They will do so by checking whether “you” performed those game actions.
NEW RULE: These instructions check whether the game action was performed, not by whom. If another player gains control of the spell or ability after the game action was performed during finalization, it will still be considered true for the purposes of these instructions.
Rules Update: Making New Choices
In the Vendetta rules update we included a model for making new choices as used by cards like Mystic Reversal and Rebuttal. We received feedback that the rules were unclear, and we clarified in the Vendetta FAQ how the interim model would work. Upon review, we found we weren’t entirely satisfied with that implementation. We decided to overhaul how new decisions are made to be simpler and more intuitive.
When making new decisions now, all decisions must be made anew. You can choose to make the same decisions as made previously, but if you’re making new decisions, you can’t go halfway.
Similar to the previous model, all decisions must be legal and valid; however, with this new model, any abilities that trigger on targeting, for example, will trigger again; even if you previously targeted the same unit. It should feel like you’re going through the process of choosing targets all over again. CLARIFIED RULE: Making new choices updated.
Rules Update: Pending Item Target Legality
Players have long wondered whether pending items are legal to target with spells and abilities. It’s very rare that such a case is possible but, like many strange rules interactions in Riftbound, we can blame these few cases on Promising Future. We figured we might as well make it clear: Pending items are not legal targets for spells and abilities. NEW RULE: Pending item target legality clarified.
Rules Update: 2v2 Scoring
The rules for 2v2 scoring were slightly contradictory. In the Vendetta rules update we cleaned them up, and in this rules update they’ve been fully aligned. Specifically, the final point and scoring eligibility special rules now apply only to teams that maintain control of a battlefield during their own or a teammate’s turn, and not during an opponent’s turn. CLARIFIED RULE: 2v2 scoring updated.
Empower Abilities

title: Core Rules: Radiance Patch Notes · Core Rules Changes (3)
officialTextEn:
Vendetta ’s Kayle, Justified needed some support from the FAQ. We’ve codified that support with the Radiance rules update. NEW RULE: Game Objects with Empower abilities may have or gain permissions to be Empowered multiple times. Such Game Objects ignore the normal “Play only if not Empowered.” restriction on Empower abilities. Note that this means you can activate the ability even if you’re at your max number of empowered statuses. That is intentional! It just does nothing. That is also intentional.
Negated and Ignored Instructions
Insightful judges and players recognized some strangeness in the rules for linked instructions from the Unleashed rules update, made more apparent by rules added in the Vendetta rules update. In the Vendetta FAQ we clarified how those rules should function, and now we’re codifying that fix into the Radiance rules update.
If an instruction mistargets, that instruction is ignored. If an instruction fails to execute for any other reason, such as it being replaced, skipped, or being impossible to perform, it is negated. Instructions that are ignored will cause any later instructions linked to them to also be ignored. If an instruction is negated, later linked instructions will not be negated; they will still execute if possible. NEW RULE: Negated and ignored instructions added.
Mandatory Requirements and Restrictions
The Vendetta FAQ clarified how Dragon Roost and other mandatory requirements functioned together. We’ve codified that into the rules in the Radiance rules update with extra clarifications. We’ve also codified the concept of a restriction: that being an effect like Perched Grimwyrm’s “Play me only to a battlefield you’ve conquered this turn.” NEW RULE: Mandatory requirements added.
NEW RULE: Restrictions added.

title: Core Rules: Radiance Patch Notes · Legacy Updates
officialTextEn:
As we’ve shared before, we’re preparing a major update to Riftbound rules with Legacy in January. To part the curtain some, this is a massive undertaking—we’re completely reformatting the rules documents to improve their readability as reference for players and judges.
We’re literally starting from the ground up, which will give us room to reduce redundant information, improve ordering, and generally clean up the rules documentation.
To be clear: this is about rewriting the rules to be more readable, and it won’t change how Riftbound’s mechanics actually work.
As always, we do not update the rules of Riftbound or introduce card errata to manage the power level of any card or effect—if we ever need to manage a powerful card, we’ll use other tools.
We’ll release an additional FAQ article after Radiance is released to further clarify remaining points of confusion for players and keep you updated as we learn more.

title: October 2026 Tournament Rules Changelog · Changing Gameplay Decisions
officialTextEn:
Before letting you dive into the nitty gritty, I want to elaborate on Riftbound’s Gameplay Decision policy (509. in the Tournament Rules).
The Gameplay Decisions policy exists to give players some flexibility when making decisions (we are not aiming for an equivalent of chess’ touch-move), but it is not meant to allow players to take back errors once their opponent is required to call information to their attention.
For example:
Player A moves their 3 Might unit to a battlefield and passes focus.
Player B indicates their 2 Might unit at that battlefield is now at 4 Might due to their legend, Wuju Bladesman.
Player A can no longer change their decision to move to that battlefield and pass focus.
High Organized Play Level (OPL) Riftbound events have the highest level of competitive integrity, valuing player’s skills and abilities to evaluate the game and make strategically correct tactical decisions. At high OPL, we never want it to feel like you need to play the game for your opponent or get punished for your opponent’s mistakes.
(At casual OPL, allowing an opponent to take back a mistake like this is not required, but it is encouraged for sportsmanship and learning.)
officialTextKo:
본격적인 세부 내용으로 들어가기에 앞서, 리프트바운드의 게임플레이 결정 규칙(대회 규정 제509조)에 대해 자세히 설명해 드리고자 합니다.
게임플레이 결정 규칙은 선수가 결정을 내릴 때 어느 정도 유연성을 부여하기 위해 존재합니다. (체스의 터치 무브와 같은 방식을 지향하는 것은 아닙니다.) 다만, 이는 상대방이 특정 정보를 지칭해야 하는 상황이 된 이후에도 선수가 자신의 실수를 되돌릴 수 있도록 허용한다는 의미는 아닙니다 .
예시:
선수 A가 3 위력 유닛을 전장으로 이동시키고 집중을 넘깁니다.
선수 B가 해당 전장에 있는 자신의 2 위력 유닛이 자신의 전설인 우주 검사로 인해 4 위력이 되었음을 알립니다.
선수 A는 해당 전장으로 이동하고 집중을 넘기기로 한 결정을 더 이상 번복할 수 없습니다.
높은 대회 등급(OPL)의 리프트바운드 대회는 최고 수준의 경쟁 공정성을 지향하며, 게임 상황을 판단하고 전략적으로 올바른 결정을 내리는 선수의 실력과 능력을 가치 있게 평가합니다. 높은 OPL에서는 선수가 상대방의 게임을 대신 플레이한다고 느끼거나 상대방의 실수 때문에 오히려 자신이 불이익을 받는 일이 없기를 바랍니다.
(캐주얼 OPL에서는 이와 같은 상대방의 실수를 되돌리도록 허용할 의무는 없지만, 스포츠맨 정신 및 학습 차원에서 권장됩니다.)

title: October 2026 Tournament Rules Changelog · Changelog
officialTextEn:
Increased clarity on when players can change gameplay decisions. Updated 509.5. - 509.6.b., renumbered following.
Completely reworked Deck Presentation Error remedies to be clearer and better describe their intent, and detail missing Chosen Champions remedies for all OPLs. Updated 703.4.b. and its sub-bullets.
Clarified that loops must be fully deterministic and include no random elements. Added examples. Added 505.2. - 505.2.b. and 505.13.
Clarified that knowingly attempting to engage in Improperly Determining a Winner is cheating, increased penalty at Professional OPL. Added 703.10.d. - 703.10.e.
Further defined Floor Judge responsibility on correcting errors they see, even if they are not called by a player. Added 204.5.c. - 204.5.c.1., renumbered following
Added clarity to when penalties should be upgraded based on being advantageous to the erroring player. Added 702.1.d. - 702.1.d.1.
Added Radiance to Standard sets. Added 601.3.c.6. - 601.3.c.6.a.
Expanded Facedown Card Error to include when cards illegally leave a facedown zone. Rewrote 702.13. and its sub-bullets.
Added Might/Might Bonus to the parts of a card that must remain intact when a card is altered. Updated 419.4.a.
Clarified that players are allowed to bluff about their private information. Added 502.11. and renumbered following.
Clarified that tokens must be represented by card objects with a clear ready state and must be understandable by opponents when used. Updated 508.8.
Clarified “choosing” things, lethal damage, and adding resources as examples of observable impact for triggers. Added 506.3.e.10. - 506.3.e.12.
Added a requirement for the state of additional turns to be communicated between players. Added 502.4.b. and renumbered following,
Clarified that when applying remedies, a “full round cycle” completes when the player whose turn the error occurred on begins their next turn. Added 702.1.e.
Added missing penalties for illegally scouting matches or using electronic devices at inappropriate times. Updated 410.4. and added 703.9.g.
Clarified that randomized deck checks should occur at the start of a round and should verify all deck elements, added some process clarification. Added 411.3.a. Updated 411.3. and renumbered following
Corrected typo in Mispayment for Cost remedy. Updated 702.9.b.3.
Fixed missing/incorrect number references. Added 602.1.a.3. Updated 406.1.d. , 702.2.b.
Clarified that Battlefields can’t be reused if a game loss is applied after Battlefields have been revealed. Added 406.1.c. and renumbered following.
Changed the Overpayment for Cost remedies to not include giving the erroring player floating resources if a simple rewind is not possible. Updated 702.8.b.1.
Clarified that players may look at outside notes during sideboarding and after Battlefields are revealed, but must stop once opening hands are drawn (before mulligans). Updated 416.4. - 416.5
Clarified that best-of-one sideboarding does not apply to limited competitions. Added 602.3.g. and renumbered following.
Clarified Failure to Maintain Game State warnings are fully exempt from upgrades. Reworded 702.1.b. and 702.1.b.1.
Added guidance for judges when performing a shuffle remedy and the deck is fully known or the randomized portion is indeterminable. Added 701.4.b.1. - 701.4.b.2.
Added special deck registration requirements for special deckbuilding rules such as Neeko. Added 401.2.a.
Updated Failure to Maintain Game State to exclude penalties covered by missed triggers. Updated 702.17.a.
Updated Chosen Champion sleeve requirements to include secret zones. Updated 422.2.b.
Clarified that 1-1 card exchange does not apply to limited sideboarding. Updated 403.4.
Removed confusing wording that implied deck registration was required at low OPL. Updated 402.1. and 703.10.b.
Clarified that at low OPL constructed events, players are typically expected to use the same deck throughout the event, unless given permission otherwise by the tournament organizer. Added 401.1.b.
Clarified that simple rewinds include ready/unrecycling runes spent on the action that is being rewound. Added 701.5.b.3.

레디언스 를 정규 세트에 추가했습니다. 제601.3.c.6조~제601.3.c.6.a조를 추가했습니다.
뒷면 표시 카드 오류 가 카드가 뒷면 표시 구역을 부적합하게 벗어나는 경우를 포함하도록 확장했습니다. 제702.13조 및 하위 조항을 다시 작성했습니다.
카드 변형 시 훼손되지 않고 유지되어야 하는 요소에 위력/추가 위력을 추가했습니다. 제419.4.a조를 업데이트했습니다.
선수가 자신의 비공개 정보를 속이는 행위가 허용됨을 명확히 했습니다. 제502.11조를 추가했으며 이후 조항 번호를 다시 지정했습니다.
토큰은 준비 상태가 명확히 구분되는 카드 오브젝트로 표시해야 하며, 이용 시 상대방이 알아볼 수 있어야 함을 명확히 했습니다. 제508.8조를 업데이트했습니다.
유발 스킬에 의해 확인 가능한 영향에서 대상 '선택', 치명적 피해 및 자원 추가 상황을 예시로 명확히 했습니다. 제506.3.e.10조~제506.3.e.12조를 추가했습니다.
추가 턴 상태를 선수 간에 공유 및 전달해야 한다는 요건을 추가했습니다. 제502.4.b조를 추가했으며 이후 조항 번호를 다시 지정했습니다.
구제책 적용 시 '전체 라운드 주기'는 오류가 발생한 턴의 선수가 자신의 다음 턴을 시작할 때 완료되는 것으로 명확히 했습니다. 제702.1.e조를 추가했습니다.
부적합한 경기 관전 또는 부적절한 시점의 전자기기 사용에 대해 누락된 페널티를 추가했습니다. 제410.4조를 업데이트했으며 제703.9.g조를 추가했습니다.
무작위 덱 점검은 라운드 시작 시점에 진행되어야 하며 모든 덱 구성 요소를 확인해야 한다는 점을 명확히 하고, 일부 절차에 대한 상세 설명을 추가했습니다. 제411.3.a조를 추가했습니다. 제411.3조를 업데이트했으며 이후 조항 번호를 다시 지정했습니다.
비용 지불 오류 구제책의 오타를 수정했습니다. 제702.9.b.3조를 업데이트했습니다.
누락되거나 잘못된 수치 표기를 수정했습니다. 제602.1.a.3조를 추가했습니다. 제406.1.d조, 제702.2.b조를 업데이트했습니다.
전장이 공개된 후 게임 패배가 적용된 경우 해당 전장을 재사용할 수 없음을 명확히 했습니다. 제406.1.c조를 추가했으며 이후 조항 번호를 다시 지정했습니다.
비용 초과 지불 구제책을 변경하여 간단한 되돌리기가 불가능할 경우, 규정 위반자에게 남은 자원을 제공하지 않도록 했습니다. 제702.8.b.1조를 업데이트했습니다.
선수가 보조 덱 사용 시 및 전장 공개 후 외부 메모를 참조할 수 있으나, 첫 손을 뽑은 순간(멀리건 이전)부터는 참조를 중단해야 함을 명확히 했습니다. 제416.4조~제416.5조를 업데이트했습니다.
단판승제 보조 덱 사용 절차는 현장 구성 대회에 적용되지 않는다는 점을 명확히 했습니다. 제602.3.g조를 추가했으며 이후 조항 번호를 다시 지정했습니다.
게임 상태 유지 실패 경고는 페널티 가중 대상에서 완전히 제외된다는 점을 명확히 했습니다. 제702.1.b조 및 제702.1.b.1조의 문구를 변경했습니다.
덱 전체가 알려져 있거나 무작위화된 부분을 특정할 수 없을 때 섞기 구제책을 수행하기 위한 심판 지침을 추가했습니다. 제701.4.b.1조~제701.4.b.2조를 추가했습니다.
니코 등 특수 덱 구성 규칙에 대한 특별 덱 등록 요건을 추가했습니다. 제401.2.a조를 추가했습니다.
게임 상태 유지 실패 를 업데이트하여 놓친 유발 스킬의 페널티를 제외하도록 했습니다. 제702.17.a.조를 업데이트했습니다.
선발 챔피언의 슬리브 요건을 비밀 구역을 포함하도록 업데이트했습니다. 제422.2.b조를 업데이트했습니다.
1대1 카드 교환 방식이 현장 구성 보조 덱에 적용되지 않는다는 점을 명확히 했습니다. 제403.4조를 업데이트했습니다.
낮은 OPL에서 덱 등록이 필요한 것으로 오인될 수 있는 문구를 삭제했습니다. 제402.1조 및 제703.10.b조를 업데이트했습니다.
낮은 OPL 사전 구성 대회에서, 대회 주최자의 별도 허가가 없는 한, 선수는 일반적으로 대회 내내 동일한 덱을 이용해야 한다는 점을 명확히 했습니다. 제401.1.b조를 추가했습니다.
간단한 되돌리기 시 되돌리려는 행동에 사용된 룬을 준비/재활용 취소 상태로 복구하는 과정이 포함된다는 점을 명확히 했습니다. 제701.5.b.3조를 추가했습니다.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 000
officialTextEn: Golden and Silver Rules

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 001
officialTextEn: Golden Rule

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 002
officialTextEn: Card text supersedes rules text. Whenever a card fundamentally contradicts the rules, the card's indication is what is true.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 050
officialTextEn: Silver Rule

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 051
officialTextEn: Card text uses different terminology than rules. Card text should be interpreted according to these rules, not as though it were text within these rules.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 052
officialTextEn: Card, when written in card effects, is shorthand for "Main Deck card." Runes, legends, and battlefields are not considered cards when executing the abilities and effects of game objects. They are considered cards for the purposes of these rules.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 053
officialTextEn: Cards refer to themselves in the first person.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 053.1
officialTextEn: * Units and legends say "I," "me," etc.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 053.2
officialTextEn: * Gear and spells say "this."

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 053.3
officialTextEn: * Battlefields say "here."

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 053.4
officialTextEn: * Cards may refer to themselves by their name for clarity. This is shorthand for the above terms.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 054
officialTextEn: “Can’t beats Can”

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 054.1
officialTextEn: Cards that forbid actions or effects, as a broad method of determination, supersede cards that allow or permit that same action or effect.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 054.2
officialTextEn: If a card specifies that an action can “only” be performed under certain circumstances, it cannot be performed under any other circumstances.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 055
officialTextEn: When executing card text, do as much as you can, ignoring impossible instructions.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 055.1
officialTextEn: If all of a card’s instructions are impossible, it is still played and resolved, but nothing happens.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 056
officialTextEn: Cards a player owns may never be placed into a non-Board zone belonging to another player.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 056.1
officialTextEn: Non-Board zones corresponding to a player include Main Deck, Rune Deck, Trash, Hand, Chosen Champion zone, and Banishment.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 056.2
officialTextEn: If a card would enter such a zone, it goes to its owner’s corresponding zone instead.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 100
officialTextEn: Game Concepts

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 101
officialTextEn: Deck Construction

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 102
officialTextEn: Riftbound is a Trading Card Game where a player must provide their own cards to play against other players.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103
officialTextEn: To play Riftbound, a player must have a Main Deck, a Rune Deck, a Champion Legend, and a number of Battlefields determined by the Mode of Play. These are collectively referred to as a player’s deck.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.1
officialTextEn: Cards in a player’s deck or rules of a Game Mode may indicate additional choices to be made while building the deck. Example: A unit reads in part “If [Name] is in your deck, choose 3 different legends in addition to your starting legend.” This decision is made while building the deck. Example: The rules of a game mode read in part “Choose an additional Chosen Champion with a different Champion Tag and Domain than your Champion Legend. Place it in the Champion Zone at the start of the game alongside your other Chosen Champion. Your deck’s Domain Identity includes that additional Chosen Champion’s Domain, if applicable.” The Chosen Champion chosen this way is decided while building the deck.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.2
officialTextEn: 1 Champion Legend

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.2.a
officialTextEn: This is placed in the Legend Zone at the start of the game.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.2.b
officialTextEn: This will dictate the Domain Identity of the deck.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.2.b.1
officialTextEn: Cards included in your deck must abide by your Domain Identity.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.2.b.2
officialTextEn: Your deck’s Domain Identity is dictated by the domains of your Champion Legend. In the default card frame, these domains appear as symbols in the legend’s upper left corner.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.2.b.3
officialTextEn: If a card has a single Domain, then that card is permitted in the Domain Identity that corresponds to the same Domain.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.2.b.4
officialTextEn: If a card has more than one Domain, then that card is permitted only in a Domain Identity that contains all of the indicated Domains on that card.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.2.b.5
officialTextEn: If a card has no Domain, then that card is permitted in decks of any Domain Identity.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.2.b.6
officialTextEn: Some Game Effects may allow a player to add cards to their deck irrespective of those cards’ Domains. Those cards are considered part of their deck’s Domain Identity, regardless of their Domain.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.3
officialTextEn: A Main Deck of at least 40 cards: A Chosen Champion Unit, as well as Units, Gear, and Spells

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.3.a
officialTextEn: Chosen Champion

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.3.a.1
officialTextEn: This will be placed in the Champion Zone at the start of the game.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.3.a.2
officialTextEn: Must be a champion unit with a champion tag that matches the tag on your Champion Legend. Example: Loose Cannon has the tag Jinx. Therefore, a player could choose Jinx, Rebel or Jinx, Demolitionist as their Chosen Champion, because they also have the tag Jinx. Example: Tibbers has the tag Annie, but it is a signature unit, not a champion unit. It cannot be your Chosen Champion, even if your Champion Legend has the tag Annie.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.3.a.3
officialTextEn: A player’s Chosen Champion is both the specific card chosen for this slot during Deck Building and also any Champion Unit with the same name as the specific card selected for this specific slot during the course of play. Example: A player chose Jinx, Rebel as their Chosen Champion. One copy of Jinx, Rebel starts the game in their Chosen Champion zone. Any additional copies of Jinx, Rebel in their Main Deck, their hand, their trash, or on the board also count as their Chosen Champion for any game rules and effects that care about Chosen Champion status during the game.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.3.b
officialTextEn: Your Main Deck can include up to 3 copies of the same named card.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.3.b.1
officialTextEn: This includes your Chosen Champion. Example: A deck could include Volibear, Furious as its Chosen Champion and still include 2 more copies of Volibear, Furious in their Main Deck.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.3.b.2
officialTextEn: Cards have different names even if they represent the same character. Example: A deck could include 3 copies of Yasuo, Remorseful and 3 copies of Yasuo, Windrider, because they have different names.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.3.c
officialTextEn: Subject to Domain Identity.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.3.d
officialTextEn: Your deck may only contain 3 total Signature cards that have the same Champion tag as your Champion Legend.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.3.d.1
officialTextEn: Regardless of name, a deck may only contain a sum total of 3 Signature cards.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.3.d.2
officialTextEn: All of the Signature cards must have the Champion tag that corresponds to the Champion Legend of the deck.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.3.d.3
officialTextEn: Signature cards are not Champion units and cannot be placed in the Champion Zone.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.3.e
officialTextEn: Subject to card legality of the Format being played.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.4
officialTextEn: Rune Deck

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.4.a
officialTextEn: 12 Rune Cards

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.4.a.1
officialTextEn: Cards in the Rune Deck must be of the Domain Identity of your Champion Legend.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.4.b
officialTextEn: Must be shuffled and kept separate from the Main Deck.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.5
officialTextEn: Battlefields

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.5.a
officialTextEn: The number will be dictated by your Mode of Play.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.5.b
officialTextEn: Subject to Domain Identity if applicable.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 103.5.c
officialTextEn: Cannot include more than one of a Battlefield of the same name when there are more than one required for the deck.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 104
officialTextEn: Setup

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 105
officialTextEn: Spaces

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 106
officialTextEn: The Play Area is a collection of logical Zones that are defined by their behaviors and relationships to Players. These Zones are grouped into The Board and Non-Board Zones.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107
officialTextEn: The Board

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107.1
officialTextEn: Bases

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107.1.a
officialTextEn: Each player has their own Base.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107.1.b
officialTextEn: Each Base is a Location. See rule 197. Locations for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107.1.c
officialTextEn: Permanents and Runes controlled by a player reside in that player's Base.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107.1.c.1
officialTextEn: Permanents attached to Permanents controlled by a player may also be found in that player’s Base, regardless of their controller.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107.1.d
officialTextEn: Permanents and Runes in Bases are Public Information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107.2
officialTextEn: Battlefield Zone

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107.2.a
officialTextEn: The Battlefield Zone houses multiple Battlefields.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107.2.b
officialTextEn: Each Battlefield is individually a Location. See rule 197. Locations for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107.2.c
officialTextEn: Battlefields and permanents at Battlefields are Public Information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107.3
officialTextEn: Facedown Zones

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107.3.a
officialTextEn: Each Battlefield is associated with a sub-zone called a Facedown Zone, a single logical space that a card can be put facedown in through various Game Effects.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107.3.b
officialTextEn: Each Facedown Zone has a maximum occupancy of one card.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107.3.b.1
officialTextEn: The maximum occupancy of a Facedown Zone can increase or decrease.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107.3.b.2
officialTextEn: If the maximum occupancy of a Facedown Zone decreases to a number less than the number of cards currently located there, the controller of that Facedown Zone must put a number of cards equal to the difference in the trash from the Facedown Zone.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107.3.c
officialTextEn: Cards can only be placed in or occupy the Facedown Zone if the controller of the card also controls the associated Battlefield.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107.3.d
officialTextEn: If a player loses Control of a Battlefield, any cards in the Facedown Zone associated with that Battlefield are removed during the next Cleanup. See rule 318. Cleanups for more information. See rule 422. Hide for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107.3.e
officialTextEn: Facedown Zones are not locations.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107.3.f
officialTextEn: Facedown Zones are Public Zones, though facedown cards located there are Private.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107.4
officialTextEn: Legend Zone

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107.4.a
officialTextEn: The space for each player's Champion Legend.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107.4.b
officialTextEn: This is not a location.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107.4.c
officialTextEn: The Champion Legend here is a Game Object. See rule 119. Game Objects for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107.4.d
officialTextEn: The Champion Legend cannot be removed, moved, or displaced from this zone.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107.4.d.1
officialTextEn: Some effects may add a legend card or token to the Legend Zone. These legends are not Champion Legends.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 107.4.d.2
officialTextEn: Non-Champion legends may be removed from the Legend Zone. They cannot exist in any zone other than the Legend Zone or Banishment.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108
officialTextEn: Non-Board Zones

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.1
officialTextEn: The Chain

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.1.a
officialTextEn: Cards and abilities are placed here as part of the process of being played. See rule 327. Chains for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.1.b
officialTextEn: Cards and abilities on the Chain are Public Information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.2
officialTextEn: Trashes

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.2.a
officialTextEn: Each player has their own Trash.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.2.b
officialTextEn: This space is where cards are placed when they are killed or discarded, when they finish being executed as spells, when they are moved to the trash as an effect, etc.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.2.c
officialTextEn: Cards in each player’s Trash are unordered. Their sequence does not matter, and they may be reorganized.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.2.d
officialTextEn: Cards in a player's Trash are Public Information. See rule 128. Privacy for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.3
officialTextEn: Champion Zones

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.3.a
officialTextEn: Each player has their own Champion Zone.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.3.b
officialTextEn: The space each player puts their Chosen Champion at the start of the game.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.3.c
officialTextEn: The Chosen Champion cannot be returned to this zone by normal means.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.3.c.1
officialTextEn: If a Chosen Champion is instructed to be returned to this zone, it can only do so if there is not a card already in this zone.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.3.d
officialTextEn: The Chosen Champion can be played from here as normal, following the rules of Playing a Card. See rule 349. Playing Cards for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.3.e
officialTextEn: Cards in a player’s Champion Zone are Public Information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.4
officialTextEn: Main Deck Zones

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.4.a
officialTextEn: Each player has their own Main Deck Zone.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.4.b
officialTextEn: The space for the player's Main Deck.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.4.c
officialTextEn: Primarily houses the face-down Main Deck during gameplay.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.4.d
officialTextEn: The number of cards in a player’s Main Deck is Public Information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.4.e
officialTextEn: The order of cards in the Main Deck is Secret Information during the course of play. See rule 128. Privacy for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.5
officialTextEn: Rune Deck Zones

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.5.a
officialTextEn: Each player has their own Rune Deck Zone.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.5.b
officialTextEn: The space for the player's Rune Deck.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.5.c
officialTextEn: Primarily houses the face-down runes during gameplay.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.5.d
officialTextEn: The order of runes in the Rune Deck is Secret Information during the course of play. See rule 128. Privacy for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.6
officialTextEn: Banishments

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.6.a
officialTextEn: Each player has their own Banishment.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.6.b
officialTextEn: This space is where cards are placed when they are banished by a spell or effect.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.6.c
officialTextEn: Represents cards that have been removed from play in a more difficult-to-recover way, or a temporary space to hold cards while effects are being processed.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.6.d
officialTextEn: The cards in the banishment are unordered. Their sequence does not matter, and they may be reorganized.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.6.e
officialTextEn: The cards in any player's Banishment are Public Information. See rule 128. Privacy for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.7
officialTextEn: The Hand

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.7.a
officialTextEn: Each player has their own Hand.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.7.b
officialTextEn: This is the zone that cards go to when Drawn.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.7.c
officialTextEn: The cards in a player's hand are Private Information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.7.d
officialTextEn: The cards in a player’s hand are Unordered. Their sequence does not matter and they may be reorganized.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.7.e
officialTextEn: The number of cards in a player's hand is Public Information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 108.7.f
officialTextEn: The hand can be targeted as a zone, and cards there can be affected by spells and effects when specified.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 109
officialTextEn: All Game Objects in the collective Play Areas are Public Information. See rule 119. Game Objects for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 109.1
officialTextEn: Any player may view, or be provided with the details of the face-up information printed on the cards in the Play Area.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 109.2
officialTextEn: The State of all Game Objects in the Play Area is also Public Information. Examples: If a Unit is Buffed If a Gear is Exhausted Etc.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 110
officialTextEn: Setup Process

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 111
officialTextEn: Each player separates their Champion Legend and places it in the Legend Zone.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 112
officialTextEn: Each player separates their Chosen Champion and places it in the Champion Zone.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 113
officialTextEn: Each player sets aside their Battlefields.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 113.1
officialTextEn: Your Mode of Play will dictate how these are used and placed into the Battlefield Zone. See rule 483. Modes of Play for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 114
officialTextEn: Each player shuffles their Main and Rune Decks, separately, then places them into their respective Zones.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 114.1
officialTextEn: The Main Deck is placed in the Main Deck Zone.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 114.2
officialTextEn: The Rune Deck is placed in the Rune Deck Zone.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 115
officialTextEn: Determine Turn Order using any fair random method agreed on by all players.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 115.1
officialTextEn: Turn Order is established as a repeating set of the players.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 115.1.a
officialTextEn: The Mode of Play will specify how to determine a First Player.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 115.1.b
officialTextEn: If not otherwise specified, Seating then determines the sequence, play proceeding clockwise from the First Player.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 115.1.b.1
officialTextEn: The First Player is the player who becomes the Turn Player first.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 115.1.c
officialTextEn: The Turn Order generates a looping queue of turns, starting with the First Player and repeating until the game ends.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 115.2
officialTextEn: See the selected Mode of Play for any adjustments to each player's first turn. See rule 483. Modes of Play for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 116
officialTextEn: Players each draw 4.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 117
officialTextEn: In turn order, players perform their Mulligan.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 117.1
officialTextEn: A player may choose up to two cards in their hand. They set those cards aside.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 117.2
officialTextEn: Then, that player draws as many cards as they set aside.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 117.3
officialTextEn: Finally, that player Recycles the cards that were set aside. See rule 417. Recycle for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 118
officialTextEn: Begin play with the First Player taking their turn.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 119
officialTextEn: Game Objects

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 120
officialTextEn: A Game Object is any game piece that can produce one or more Game Effects or grant prerequisites for players to take Game Actions.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 121
officialTextEn: A Game Object does not include nor preclude any inherent properties beyond the ability to produce, or act as the prerequisite for, Game Effects and Game Actions.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 122
officialTextEn: A Game Object can be a literal object or a logical object.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 123
officialTextEn: Game Objects include, but are not limited to, the following: Main Deck cards in any zone Runes in any zone Legends Battlefields Tokens in any zone Abilities of any type on the chain Counters and other status markers

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 124
officialTextEn: A Game Object that changes zones to or from a Non-Board Zone becomes a new object for the purposes of tracking that object.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 124.1
officialTextEn: Whenever a Game Object changes zones to or from a Non-Board Zone, all Temporary Modifications of all kinds cease to be tracked on it in all capacities. Examples: Damage is cleared. Counters are removed. Granted Keywords are no longer granted. Statuses are cleared.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 124.2
officialTextEn: A Game Object can have any of the following statuses (non-exhaustive): Attached, Attacking, Buffed, Banished, Controlled, Defending, Empowered, Equipped, Exhausted, Facedown, Readied, Replaced, Revealed, Stunned, and any applied Layer effects.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 125
officialTextEn: Cards

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 126
officialTextEn: Riftbound games are composed of players playing the cards in their respective decks.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 127
officialTextEn: Ownership

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 127.1
officialTextEn: For gameplay purposes, a card's Owner is the player who brought it into the game, either as their Champion Legend, one of their Battlefields, as part of their Main Deck or Rune Deck, or Created during the process of play. The legal owner of a card doesn't matter during gameplay. Example: Bo didn't bring a deck, so Alice loans him a deck. During the game, Bo is considered the owner of those cards, even though legally they belong to Alice.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 128
officialTextEn: Privacy

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 128.1
officialTextEn: A card will always exist in one of the many Zones described during Setup.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 128.2
officialTextEn: A card will have a different level of Privacy based on its state or where it resides at a given time.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 128.2.a
officialTextEn: Unless specified otherwise by the state of the card, a card’s Privacy is the same as the zone it is located in.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 128.3
officialTextEn: Secret: This level of Privacy indicates that no player may read or look at the face of the card.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 128.4
officialTextEn: Private: This level of Privacy indicates that only the controller of a card on the board or the owner of a card in any other zone may read or look at the face of the card. Example: Cards in a player's hand are owned by that player. Only that player may read or look at their faces. Example: If a player controls a facedown card at a battlefield, that player and only that player may read or look at that card's face, regardless of who owns that card.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 128.5
officialTextEn: Public: This level of Privacy indicates that any player may read or look at the face of the card.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 128.6
officialTextEn: A player cannot be compelled to perform an action on cards whose privacy is secret or private if that action specifies a type or quality of card. Example: A card effect reads, “Play a unit from your hand, ignoring its costs.” Although the effect does not say “may”, the player can choose not to perform the action even if they have a unit in their hand, because the effect specifies a card type.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 128.6.a
officialTextEn: If an effect would compel a player to perform an action on cards whose privacy is secret or private, and if that effect specifies a type or quality of card, the player in question may choose to ignore that instruction. Ignored instructions are deemed impossible.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 129
officialTextEn: Back Side

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 129.1
officialTextEn: The back side of a card is the side with the Riftbound logo.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 129.2
officialTextEn: There is a unique pattern of back side for each of the three categories of card: Main Deck cards, Rune Deck cards, and Battlefields and Champion Legends.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 129.3
officialTextEn: The back side of a card is presented to conceal information for Private and Secret information cards. For example, cards in the Main Deck and cards in hand have their back side presented.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 129.4
officialTextEn: The term facedown is used to describe the state during regular play of having a card's back side presented on the Board. A facedown card’s front side is considered Private Information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 130
officialTextEn: Front Side

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 130.1
officialTextEn: The front side of a card is the opposite of its back.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 130.2
officialTextEn: This is also referred to as a front face.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 130.3
officialTextEn: This can be identified in situations where the back is not easily discernible by the presence of the Play Cost in the upper left corner of the card.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 130.4
officialTextEn: Cards, when played, are played with their front face presented.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 130.5
officialTextEn: The term face up is used to describe the state during regular play of having a card's front face presented

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 130.6
officialTextEn: Cards are considered to be Public Information while in this state, even if obscured by other cards in a pile. Example: The Trash is Public Information because all cards there have their front face presented even while stacked.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 131
officialTextEn: Cost

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 131.1
officialTextEn: Main Deck cards have a Cost, listed in the upper left corner of the front face of the card. See rule 165. Rune Pools for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 131.2
officialTextEn: Energy Cost

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 131.2.a
officialTextEn: The numeral listed in the Cost element in the upper left corner of the card.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 131.3
officialTextEn: Power cost

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 131.3.a
officialTextEn: The symbols, listed vertically, in the Cost element in the upper left corner of the card.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 131.3.b
officialTextEn: This section may not be present on every card.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 132
officialTextEn: Name

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 132.1
officialTextEn: Each card has a name that identifies it uniquely.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 132.2
officialTextEn: This is usually located in the middle of the card.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 132.3
officialTextEn: Cards that are printed in different languages but represent the same card are considered to have the same name for the purposes of deckbuilding and gameplay. Example: Chemtech Enforcer in English and its counterpart in Chinese are considered the same card, despite the Name element on the card reading differently.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 132.4
officialTextEn: Some cards have both a short name and a subtitle. For all purposes, including rules and deckbuilding, such a card’s name is “[Short Name], [Subtitle]”. Example: Kai’Sa, Evolutionary and Kai’Sa, Survivor both have the short name Kai’Sa, but they have different names. You can include 3 of each in your deck under normal deckbuilding rules. If one of them is your Chosen Champion, the other is not.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 133
officialTextEn: Category

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 133.1
officialTextEn: A card can have one or more Categories and Sub-Categories based on the properties of its front and back sides.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 133.2
officialTextEn: These Categories and Sub-Categories dictate the behaviors of the card during play.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 133.3
officialTextEn: Spells and other effects can refer to categories, sub-categories, supertypes, card types, tags, and other characteristics inclusively or exclusively. Example: A "non-unit card" is any card that is not a unit. Example: A "unit" is any game object that is a unit, regardless of any other categories it belongs to.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 133.3.a
officialTextEn: When characteristics are referred to in this way, it refers to any Game Object with the appropriate characteristic on the board, unless the zone is specified implicitly or explicitly by the effect doing the referring or the nature of the characteristic. Example: A "Yeti" refers to a game object with the Yeti tag on the board. Example: A "spell" refers to a spell on the chain, because spells cannot exist as game objects on the board. Example: A "spell in your trash" refers to a spell card in your trash because the effect specifies the zone in question.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 133.4
officialTextEn: Main Deck Cards begin the game in the Main Deck or (in the case of a Chosen Champion) the Champion Zone.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 133.4.a
officialTextEn: Permanents

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 133.4.a.1
officialTextEn: An umbrella sub-category encompassing Main Deck Game Objects that remain on the board after being played.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 133.4.a.2
officialTextEn: Unit and Gear are permanent types.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 133.4.b
officialTextEn: Spells

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 133.4.b.1
officialTextEn: A sub-category encompassing Main Deck cards with the spell type, which do not remain on the board after being played.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 133.5
officialTextEn: Rune Deck Cards begin the game in the Rune Deck.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 133.5.a
officialTextEn: Runes

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 133.5.a.1
officialTextEn: A sub-category encompassing cards with the rune type. These are channeled rather than played. They remain on the board after being channeled, but they are not permanents, as they are not Main Deck cards.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 133.6
officialTextEn: Other Cards are not part of either the Main or Rune Decks and begin the game in a zone determined by their type.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 133.6.a
officialTextEn: Battlefields

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 133.6.a.1
officialTextEn: A sub-category encompassing cards with the battlefield type. They are not played or channeled. They start the game on the board.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 133.6.b
officialTextEn: Legends

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 133.6.b.1
officialTextEn: A sub-category encompassing cards with the legend type. They are not played or channeled. They start the game in the Legend Zone and cannot typically leave it during play.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 133.7
officialTextEn: Supertypes are Categories that may apply to game objects of multiple types. They are listed before a card’s type.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 133.7.a
officialTextEn: Champion is a supertype that applies exclusively to units. It impacts the rules for deckbuilding. See rule 103.2.a. Chosen Champion for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 133.7.b
officialTextEn: Signature is a supertype that may apply to game objects of any card type. It impacts the rules for deckbuilding. See rule 103.2.d. for more information about Signature cards.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 133.8
officialTextEn: Tags are Categories that may apply to game objects of multiple types. They are listed after a card’s type.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 133.8.a
officialTextEn: Tags have no innate rules meaning, but may be referenced by game rules and card effects.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 133.8.b
officialTextEn: Tags used to link Legends, Champion Units, and Signature cards are known as Champion Tags.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 134
officialTextEn: Domain

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 134.1
officialTextEn: Most cards belong to one or more of six Domains, identified by one or more symbols in the lower right corner.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 134.2
officialTextEn: Each Domain has an associated color, a unique symbol, and a shorthand used to represent that symbol in written text.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 134.2.a
officialTextEn: Fury is associated with the color red and represented by a circular symbol with three projecting points. Its shorthand is [R].

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 134.2.b
officialTextEn: Calm is associated with the color green and represented by a symbol resembling a leaf. Its shorthand is [G].

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 134.2.c
officialTextEn: Mind is associated with the color blue and represented by a symbol resembling a sun and moon. Its shorthand is [B].

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 134.2.d
officialTextEn: Body is associated with the color orange and represented by a blocky diamond-shaped symbol. Its shorthand is [O].

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 134.2.e
officialTextEn: Chaos is associated with the color purple and represented by a hexagonal symbol with swirls emanating from its center. Its shorthand is [P].

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 134.2.f
officialTextEn: Order is associated with the color yellow and represented by an angular winged symbol. Its shorthand is [Y].

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135
officialTextEn: Rules Text

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.1
officialTextEn: All cards have a section that describes how they affect the game. This section is known as the Rules Text of the card.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2
officialTextEn: This section may contain:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.a
officialTextEn: Abilities

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.a.1
officialTextEn: Abilities are discrete pieces of text that describe what a card may or must do. See rule 360. Abilities for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.a.2
officialTextEn: They may appear on any card.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.b
officialTextEn: Instructions

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.b.1
officialTextEn: Instructions are a type of text that appears on spells and within abilities.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.b.2
officialTextEn: They describe actions to be performed by one or more players.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.b.3
officialTextEn: Instructions will self-describe when they are to be executed. If there is no timing described, they will execute during resolution. Example: An instruction says “as you play me, kill a unit as an additional cost.” That instruction will execute as the card is being played. If the card is given Repeat and the Repeat cost is paid, this instruction will not execute because the Repeat execution does not happen until resolution of the spell, after this instruction has executed.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.b.4
officialTextEn: Instructions can usually be recognized by the way they are written. An instruction is written in the imperative mood, using the base form of a verb and omitting the subject unless necessary.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.b.5
officialTextEn: A single instruction is made up of a game action and its complement.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.b.5.a
officialTextEn: The complement of a game action is made up of the players or Game Objects that perform that game action, that that game action is performed on, the condition under which it is performed, and the duration for its effect to last. Some game actions omit a complement entirely. Example: Void Seeker is made up of two instructions. The first is “deal 4 to a unit at a battlefield.” Here “deal 4” is the game action, while “a unit at a battlefield,” is its complement. The second instruction, “draw 1,” has no complement. Example: Teemo, Strategist’s defend trigger reads “When I defend, choose an enemy unit here and reveal the top 5 cards of your Main Deck. Deal 1 to that unit for each card with Hidden revealed this way, then recycle the revealed cards.” There are four instructions here: “choose an enemy unit here,” “reveal the top 5 cards of your Main Deck,” “deal 1 to that unit for each card with Hidden revealed this way,” and “recycle the revealed cards.”

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.b.5.b
officialTextEn: If a conditional clause appears in instructions prior to one or more clauses with multiple instructions, that condition applies to all instructions in subsequent clauses in the same sentence. Example: A spell reads in part “If you’ve gained a point this turn, draw 1, then discard 1.” In order for either of the instructions that follow the “If you’ve gained a point this turn,” conditional clause to execute, the condition must be true. Example: Rogue Assassin is a legend that reads in part “[Action][>] [E]: If it's your turn, move a friendly unit in a showdown to base and if I'm [Empowered], ready it.” The first conditional clause in the activated ability applies to all subsequent instructions in the same sentence. The second conditional clause, “if I’m [Empowered],” only applies to the instruction that immediately follows it.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.b.6
officialTextEn: Instructions do not include trigger conditions or the events or actions that a replacement effect defines as being eligible to be replaced.
