Example: An ability reads “When you play me, draw 1.” The trigger condition for this ability is not an instruction. “Draw 1,” is the only instruction included in the ability. Example: An ability reads “If a unit would die, banish it instead.” The text “If a unit would die,” is not an instruction of the ability. Example: An ability reads “As I’m revealed from your Main Deck, Add [2].” The text “As I’m revealed from your Main Deck,” is not an instruction of the ability.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.b.7
officialTextEn: Instructions of a spell or ability may reference actions taken during Finalization. They will do so by checking whether “you” performed those game actions. These instructions check whether the game action was performed, not by whom. If another player gains control of the spell or ability after the game action was performed during finalization, it will still be considered true for the purposes of these instructions. Example: Rampage is a spell that reads “As you play this, you may pay [C] as an additional cost.” and “Choose a friendly unit and an enemy unit. If you paid the additional cost, give the friendly unit +2 [Might] this turn. They deal damage equal to their Mights to each other.” If another player gains control of Rampage, although they are not the one who paid the cost, the “if you paid the additional cost,” condition will still be fulfilled. Example: Back Off is a spell that reads in part “If you played this from your hand, draw 1.” On resolution, Back Off checks if it was played from hand. If another player gained control of Back Off, as long as the card was played from hand, the condition will be true and the controller of the spell will draw 1.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.c
officialTextEn: Keywords

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.c.1
officialTextEn: Keywords are short words or phrases that represent longer abilities or instructions. See rule 800. Keywords for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.c.2
officialTextEn: Keywords may or may not have reminder text.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.d
officialTextEn: Reminder Text

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.d.1
officialTextEn: Reminder text appears in italics and parentheses.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.d.2
officialTextEn: Its purpose is to summarize relevant rules, including keywords and other rules.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.d.3
officialTextEn: The presence, absence, or exact wording of reminder text has no effect on game function.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.e
officialTextEn: Symbols

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.e.1
officialTextEn: Rules text sometimes contains symbols that express game concepts. Each symbol also has a shorthand used to represent it in written text.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.e.2
officialTextEn: The cost of Exhausting a Permanent is represented by the “exhaust symbol,” which resembles a card turning sideways. Its shorthand is [E]. (Some previous rules information has given its shorthand as [T].)

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.e.3
officialTextEn: Might is represented by the “Might symbol,” which resembles a sword and shield. Its shorthand is [M]. (Some previous rules information has given its shorthand as [S].)

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.e.4
officialTextEn: Power of a specific Domain is represented by its domain symbol and the corresponding shorthand. See rule 134. Domain for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.e.5
officialTextEn: Power of any Domain is represented by a swirling rainbow symbol. Its shorthand is [A].

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.e.5.a
officialTextEn: When required as a cost, [A] can be paid by Power of any Domain.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.e.5.b
officialTextEn: When Added to a player’s Rune Pool, [A] can be spent to pay a Power cost of any Domain.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.e.6
officialTextEn: Power of a domain corresponding to a card’s own Domain is not represented by a symbol, but appears in these rules similarly to other symbols. Its shorthand is [C].

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.e.6.a
officialTextEn: When a [C] shorthand is printed on a card as reminder text, it assumes that card’s usual Domain, but it still means “one Power of this card’s Domain.”

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.e.6.b
officialTextEn: A [C] shorthand on a card with no Domain is processed as [A] instead.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.e.6.c
officialTextEn: A [C] shorthand on a card with multiple Domains is processed as any power of that card’s Domains. Example: Defiant Dance is a Calm and Chaos spell. Its cost is [1][C]. The power component of that cost can be paid with either [G] or [P]. Example: Tibbers is a Fury and Chaos Unit. If Tibbers is granted the Accelerate keyword, the power component of the optional additional cost can be paid with either [R] or [P].

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.e.7
officialTextEn: A keyword associated with an ability is indicated by the [>] symbol.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.e.7.a
officialTextEn: This could be a dependent keyword like [Legion][>] or [Level][>], a triggered ability with a keyworded trigger condition like [Deathknell] or it could be a permissive keyword associated with an ability like [Action][>] or [Reaction][>].

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.2.e.7.b
officialTextEn: Whatever instruction or ability comes after the [>] is modified by the keyword that comes before the [>]. It will either be inactive, in the case of a dependent keyword; the trigger effect, in the case of a keyword triggered ability; or it will receive the permission granted by the keyword in the case of a permissive keyword.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.3
officialTextEn: Rules text can be blank.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.4
officialTextEn: A card’s printed Rules Text is Inactive while that card is Attached to another card. See rule 716. Attachment for more information. See rule 720. Inactive for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.4.a
officialTextEn: The presence of text, rules, Keywords, and other effects can still be referenced and detected by other game effects, even while Rules Text is Inactive.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 135.4.b
officialTextEn: Any granted or appended Rules Text on a card is still Active even if that card is Attached to another card.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 136
officialTextEn: Effect Text

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 136.1
officialTextEn: Some cards have a separate section of text below the Rules Text. This is referred to as the Effect Text.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 136.2
officialTextEn: Effect Text can contain additional Abilities.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 136.2.a
officialTextEn: Effect Text can be blank.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 136.2.b
officialTextEn: Effect Text is inactive unless the card with the Effect Text is Attached to another card. See rule 716. Attachment for more information. See rule 720. Inactive for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 136.2.c
officialTextEn: The abilities in the Effect Text section of a card are appended to the Rules Text of the card to which the card with the Effect Text is Attached.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 136.2.d
officialTextEn: Effect Text may refer to “this” or to the name of the Attached game object that appended the Effect Text. Doing so refers to the Attached game object and not the Top-Most Card, even if the Top-Most Card shares a name with the Attached game object. Example: Guardian Angel’s effect text reads “If I would die, kill Guardian Angel instead. Heal me, exhaust me, and recall me.” Example: Brutalizer’s effect text reads “If this was attached to me this turn, I have an additional +2 [M].” The “this” in the effect text refers to the attached Brutalizer.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 137
officialTextEn: Might Bonus

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 137.1
officialTextEn: Some cards have a Might Bonus in their lower right corner, expressed as an operator plus an integer.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 137.2
officialTextEn: A card’s Might Bonus can be +0.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 137.3
officialTextEn: A card’s Might Bonus modulates the Might of the card to which the card that has the Might Bonus is Attached. See rule 716. Attachment for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 137.3.a
officialTextEn: The Might Bonus is applied while Attached and stops applying as soon as the card with the Might Bonus is no longer Attached.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 137.3.b
officialTextEn: If the card to which a card with a Might Bonus is Attached has no Might value, the Might Bonus is ignored.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 138
officialTextEn: Flavor Text

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 138.1
officialTextEn: Flavor text is text that appears at the bottom of some cards to provide aesthetic enjoyment. It conveys no gameplay information. Example: The card Void Seeker features a quote from the character Kai'Sa. It does not have the Kai'Sa tag and has no gameplay connection to the Champion unit Kai'Sa.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 138.2
officialTextEn: Flavor text is located at the bottom of the section provided for rules text, usually in a shaded bar. It appears in italics.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 139
officialTextEn: Illustration

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 139.1
officialTextEn: Each card has an illustration. It conveys no gameplay information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 140
officialTextEn: Units

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 141
officialTextEn: Unit is:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 141.1
officialTextEn: A Game Object

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 141.1.a
officialTextEn: While on the Board:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 141.1.a.1
officialTextEn: Units are at one of several Locations while on the Board: a Battlefield or their Base.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 141.1.a.2
officialTextEn: Units and their details are Public Information while on the Board.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 141.1.a.3
officialTextEn: Units can be chosen, affected, or manipulated by spells, affects, or game actions that specify Units.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 141.1.a.4
officialTextEn: Units can be Killed. See rule 429. Kill for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 141.1.b
officialTextEn: While in the Trash:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 141.1.b.1
officialTextEn: Units are treated as Cards, similar to when in the Hand.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 141.1.b.2
officialTextEn: They retain the properties of being a Unit, but are not on the Board and thus cannot take actions or be affected by spells, abilities, or game actions that target Units on the Board.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 141.1.b.3
officialTextEn: Units can be affected by spells and game effects that target Units in the Trash.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 141.2
officialTextEn: A Card Type

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 141.2.a
officialTextEn: This is a unique identifier that some spells or abilities will use to restrict what they can choose or affect.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 141.2.b
officialTextEn: The card type is relevant in all zones.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 142
officialTextEn: Damage is a marked value that is applied to Units.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 142.1
officialTextEn: Damage is not a Game Object.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 142.2
officialTextEn: Damage is a value tracked per-Unit.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 142.3
officialTextEn: Damage is marked on Units by players.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 142.3.a
officialTextEn: The player responsible for the Deal action that caused the Damage to be marked is the player who marked that Damage.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 142.3.b
officialTextEn: Game Effects may refer to that player’s Damage. This means the Damage marked by that player. Example: A unit reads in part “Your damage can’t be prevented.” This refers to the damage marked by that player.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 142.4
officialTextEn: Damage tracks how close a Unit is to being Killed. See rule 429. Kill for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 142.4.a
officialTextEn: Lethal Damage is the amount of marked Damage that will cause a unit to die in a cleanup.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 142.4.b
officialTextEn: Lethal Damage for a Unit is a non-zero amount greater than or equal to that Unit’s Might. Example: A unit has 5 [M] and 3 damage marked on it. Frigid Touch is played targeting that unit. When it resolves, the unit’s Might becomes 3, and it will have lethal damage marked on it. Example: A unit has 0 [M]. In order to have lethal damage marked on it, it must have at least 1 damage marked on it.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 142.4.c
officialTextEn: Some effects may alter this amount. These effects will refer to the amount of damage needed to kill a unit. Example: Elder Dragon’s passive ability reads “Any amount of your damage is enough to kill enemy units.” This alters the Lethal Damage value for enemy units that have damage marked by you.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 142.5
officialTextEn: Damage can be Healed. See rule 419. Heal for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 143
officialTextEn: Units have multiple Intrinsic Properties unique to them:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 143.1
officialTextEn: Tag: A Unit has zero or more Tags representing one or more champions, regions, factions, or species it belongs to.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 143.1.a
officialTextEn: These have no intrinsic rules or behaviors by themselves.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 143.1.b
officialTextEn: Spells, abilities, and game actions can reference these types as part of their execution.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 143.2
officialTextEn: Might: The combat statistic of a Unit. Used to determine a Unit's contribution to Combat, as well as when it is Killed by damaging effects.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 143.2.a
officialTextEn: A Unit’s Might can be referenced by cards and effects in one of three forms: A Unit has a Printed Might, that is the value in the top right corner of the unit card/token; a Base Might, that is a trait that is alterable by effects in the Trait-Altering layer; and an Effective Might, that is the value calculated in the arithmetic layer including all Might altering Game Effects. See rule 475. Layers for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 143.2.a.1
officialTextEn: Card text may refer to the latter two of these three forms. When cards or these rules refer to a Unit’s Effective Might, they will do so by simply referring to that unit’s “Might.” Example: A card reads in part “Choose a unit. Its base Might becomes 5 this turn.” This applies an effect in the trait-altering layer. Example: A card reads in part “Choose a unit. Increase its Might to 5 this turn.” This applies an effect in the arithmetic layer.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 143.2.b
officialTextEn: If a Unit ever has nonzero damage marked on it equalling or exceeding its Might, it is Killed.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 143.2.c
officialTextEn: If a unit's Might is ever less than 0, it is treated as 0 when referenced by spells and abilities, and when summing Might to be assigned as damage in the Combat Damage Step. See rule 467. The Combat Damage Step for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 143.2.c.1
officialTextEn: Although the unit’s Might is treated as 0, it is not 0. Effects that calculate Might increases and decreases use the actual value of the unit’s Might.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 143.3
officialTextEn: Units can have damage marked on them.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 143.3.a
officialTextEn: When spells, abilities, or other game effects deal damage, Units mark that damage on them temporarily. This can be tracked with coins, dice, or other markers, or by memory.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 143.3.b
officialTextEn: Damage is Healed from Units at two specific times:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 143.3.b.1
officialTextEn: At the end of each player's turn. See rule 317.2. Ending Phase for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 143.3.b.2
officialTextEn: During a Combat Cleanup. See rule 468.1. for more information about Combat Cleanups.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 143.4
officialTextEn: Units enter the Board exhausted.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 143.4.a
officialTextEn: This can be altered by Accelerate or similar game effects. See rule 805. Accelerate for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 143.5
officialTextEn: Units cannot be Attached to other permanents. See rule 435. Attach for more information on the attach game action. See rule 716. Attachment for more information on attachment.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 143.5.a
officialTextEn: If a Unit would be Attached to a permanent, nothing happens.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 143.5.b
officialTextEn: If a non-Unit Game Object that is Attached becomes a Unit through any means, it detaches as it becomes a Unit.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 144
officialTextEn: Units have the Inherent Ability to perform a Standard Move.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 144.1
officialTextEn: This action is limited in when it can be performed.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 144.1.a
officialTextEn: This action can be done any time during a player's Main Phase.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 144.1.b
officialTextEn: This action cannot be performed during a Closed State.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 144.1.c
officialTextEn: This action cannot be performed during a Showdown or Combat.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 144.2
officialTextEn: Exhausting the Unit is the Cost for this action.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 144.3
officialTextEn: Players may perform multiple Units' standard move simultaneously. This is treated as one game action performed on multiple Units.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 144.3.a
officialTextEn: When a Move like this is declared by a player, the units' Destination must be the same.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 144.3.b
officialTextEn: When a Move like this is declared by a player, the Origins do not need to be the same.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 144.3.c
officialTextEn: The Costs of Exhausting the Units are also paid Simultaneously.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 144.4
officialTextEn: The Destinations where Units can Move to with their Standard Move are restricted:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 144.4.a
officialTextEn: Units may move from their Base to a Battlefield.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 144.4.a.1
officialTextEn: Units cannot Move to a Battlefield that already has units from 2 other players present, or where a Combat is ongoing that has 2 other players as participants. See rule 449.2. For more information on valid destinations for movement.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 144.4.b
officialTextEn: Units may move from a Battlefield to their Base.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 144.4.c
officialTextEn: Ganking is a unique ability that affects a Unit's Standard Move

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 144.4.c.1
officialTextEn: Units with Ganking may use their Standard Move to Move from Battlefield to Battlefield. See rule 810. Ganking for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 145
officialTextEn: Units may have Activated Abilities.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 145.1
officialTextEn: Activated Abilities are Game Effects that are written as Costs followed by a ":", and then succeeded by an effect. See rule 376. Activated Abilities for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 145.2
officialTextEn: The Activated Ability of Units may be executed at any time during the controlling player's Main Phase during an Open State, and not during a Showdown.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 145.2.a
officialTextEn: This follows the same process as playing a card. See rule 349. Playing Cards for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 145.2.a.1
officialTextEn: This behaves, once activated, like a spell without an associated card.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 146
officialTextEn: Units have a Location.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 146.1
officialTextEn: A Unit’s Location is the Base or Battlefield it currently occupies. See rule 197. Locations for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 147
officialTextEn: Gear

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 148
officialTextEn: Gear are:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 148.1
officialTextEn: A Game Object

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 148.1.a
officialTextEn: While on the Board.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 148.1.a.1
officialTextEn: Gear can only be played to a player's Base unless an effect specifies otherwise.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 148.1.a.2
officialTextEn: Gear and their details are Public Information while on the Board.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 148.1.a.3
officialTextEn: Gear can be chosen, affected, or manipulated by spells, effects, or game actions that specify Gear.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 148.1.a.4
officialTextEn: Gear can be Killed. See rule 429. Kill for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 148.1.b
officialTextEn: While in the Trash

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 148.1.b.1
officialTextEn: Gear are treated as Cards before Game Objects, similar to the Hand.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 148.1.b.2
officialTextEn: They retain the properties of being Gear, but are not on the Board and thus cannot take actions or be affected by spells, abilities, or game actions that affect Gear on the Board.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 148.1.b.3
officialTextEn: Gear can be affected by spells and game effects that affect Gear in the Trash.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 148.2
officialTextEn: A Card Type

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 148.2.a
officialTextEn: This is a unique identifier that some spells or abilities will use to restrict what they can choose or affect.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 148.2.b
officialTextEn: The card type is relevant in all zones.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 149
officialTextEn: Gear have several Intrinsic Properties unique to them.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 149.1
officialTextEn: Gear enter play Ready.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 149.2
officialTextEn: Gear can only be played to a player's Base unless an effect specifies otherwise.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 149.3
officialTextEn: If an unattached non-Unit Gear is at a Battlefield or in another player’s base for any reason during a cleanup, then it is recalled to its controller's Base as a corrective action. See rule 456. Recalls for more information. See rule 318. Cleanups for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 150
officialTextEn: Gear can have the Equipment tag.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 150.1
officialTextEn: These Gear are referred to as Equipment.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 150.2
officialTextEn: Equipment have effect text and a Might bonus. See rule 136. Effect Text for more information on effect text. See rule 137. Might Bonus for more information on Might bonuses.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 150.3
officialTextEn: Equipment can have the Equip or Quick-Draw keywords. See rule 818. Equip for more information on the Equip keyword. See rule 819. Quick-Draw for more information on the Quick-Draw keyword.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 150.4
officialTextEn: Equipment are still Gear and have the same intrinsic properties and rules that Gear do.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 150.5
officialTextEn: Equipment and whether a Gear has the Equipment tag is a characteristic of the Gear may be checked or referenced by other Game Effects.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 151
officialTextEn: Gear may have Activated Abilities.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 151.1
officialTextEn: Activated Abilities are Game Effects that are written as Costs followed by a ":", and then succeeded by an effect. See rule 376. Activated Abilities for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 151.2
officialTextEn: The Activated Ability of Gear may be executed at any time during the controlling player's Main Phase during an Open State, and not during a Showdown.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 151.2.a
officialTextEn: This follows the same process as playing a card. See rule 349. Playing Cards for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 151.2.a.1
officialTextEn: This behaves, once activated, like a spell without an associated card.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 152
officialTextEn: Gear have a Location.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 152.1
officialTextEn: A Gear’s Location is the Base or Battlefield it currently occupies. See rule 197. Locations for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 152.2
officialTextEn: Non-Unit Gear cannot normally become located at a Battlefield unless by some special means. Example: Gear are played to Base unless an effect specifies otherwise. A gear played from Facedown, which is specified to be played to the Battlefield it was played from, will enter at that Battlefield. Gear can also become located at a Battlefield if they are attached to a unit who becomes located at a Battlefield. A Gear that is a Unit can move to a Battlefield. See rule 811. Hidden for more information. See rule 716. Attachment for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 153
officialTextEn: Spells

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 154
officialTextEn: Spell is a card type.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 155
officialTextEn: A spell can be played during an Open State outside of Showdowns on its controller's turn.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 156
officialTextEn: A spell is controlled by the player who played it.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 157
officialTextEn: A spell creates a game effect according to its instructions and is then placed in the Trash of the player who owns it.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 158
officialTextEn: When a spell is successfully played, a player executes the rules text of the spell. This is called Resolving the spell.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 158.1
officialTextEn: Spells have their rules text executed from top to bottom when they are Resolved.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 158.2
officialTextEn: If a later part of a spell applies a Replacement Effect that alters earlier parts of the spell, apply those replacement effects as appropriate. Example: A spell says "Choose a unit. Kill it the next time it takes damage this turn." and "[Legion] — Kill it now instead." If the Legion condition is satisfied, the unit is killed immediately and the instruction to kill it the next time it takes damage is negated, even if the unit remains on the board somehow. See rule 367. Replacement Effects for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 158.3
officialTextEn: While a spell or ability on the chain is Resolving, no other spells or abilities can be finalized on the chain or resolved, including triggered abilities or game effects that would occur as a result of the execution of the spell.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 158.3.a
officialTextEn: Finish resolving all effects of a spell before addressing any chain items or Tasks the spell may have added or made outstanding through execution.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 159
officialTextEn: Certain Keywords on spells are not executable rules text, but instead intrinsic properties of the spell.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 159.1
officialTextEn: These determine inherent properties and behaviors of the spell before being played or while on the chain.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 159.2
officialTextEn: These keywords are:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 159.2.a
officialTextEn: Action

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 159.2.a.1
officialTextEn: This indicates that, in addition to being able to be played during an Open State, this spell may also be played during Open States during Showdowns. See rule 806. Action for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 159.2.b
officialTextEn: Reaction

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 159.2.b.1
officialTextEn: Grants all cases and rules of Action.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 159.2.b.2
officialTextEn: In addition to all prior cases, may also be played during all forms of Closed State.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 159.2.b.3
officialTextEn: This will result in this spell resolving before spells and abilities that are already on the chain. See rule 813. Reaction for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 160
officialTextEn: Runes

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 161
officialTextEn: Rune is a Card Type.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 161.1
officialTextEn: A Rune is not a Main Deck card.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 161.1.a
officialTextEn: This means, despite remaining on the Board until Recycled or otherwise removed from the board, it is not a Permanent.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 161.2
officialTextEn: Runes are kept in the Rune Deck.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 161.2.a
officialTextEn: Exactly 12 Rune cards chosen during Deck Construction. See rule 103.3. Rune Deck for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 161.2.b
officialTextEn: When a Rune is Recycled it is returned to the Rune Deck, not the Main Deck. See rule 417. Recycle for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 162
officialTextEn: Runes produce the resources needed to pay costs.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 163
officialTextEn: Runes produce Energy and Power.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 163.1
officialTextEn: Energy is used to pay numeric Energy costs.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 163.1.a
officialTextEn: Energy has no Domain.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 163.1.b
officialTextEn: Energy has no type.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 163.2
officialTextEn: Power is used to pay Domain-associated Power Costs.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 163.2.a
officialTextEn: Power has a Domain.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 163.2.a.1
officialTextEn: Power's Domain usually corresponds to the Domain of the Rune that produced it.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 163.2.b
officialTextEn: Some Power is Universal and can be used to pay for costs of any Domain.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 164
officialTextEn: Basic Runes

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 164.1
officialTextEn: There are six Basic Runes, each with a Domain corresponding to its name: Fury Rune Calm Rune Mind Rune Body Rune Chaos Rune Order Rune

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 164.2
officialTextEn: A Basic Rune always has the following two Abilities:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 164.2.a
officialTextEn: [Reaction][>] [E]: Add [1].

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 164.2.b
officialTextEn: [Reaction][>] Recycle this: Add [C].

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 164.2.b.1
officialTextEn: The Power added this way corresponds to the Domain of the Rune that is being Recycled.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 165
officialTextEn: Rune Pools

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 166
officialTextEn: The Rune Pool is a conceptual collection of a player's available Energy and Power available to pay Costs.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 166.1
officialTextEn: When a card adds Energy or Power, it is added to the controlling player's Rune Pool.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 166.2
officialTextEn: Players must add Energy and Power to their Rune Pool in order to be able to spend it to play cards or pay for Abilities with costs.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 166.3
officialTextEn: Energy and Power do not have a physical marker or tracker, although players may wish to use a physical tracker if they are retaining unspent Energy and Power over the course of their turn.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 167
officialTextEn: Every player's Rune Pool empties at the start of each player's Main Phase and the end of each player's turn.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 167.1
officialTextEn: Any unspent Energy or Power are lost.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 168
officialTextEn: All Abilities that include the action "Add" are abilities that are adding Energy or Power to the Rune Pool. See rule 430. Add for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 169
officialTextEn: Battlefields

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 170
officialTextEn: Battlefields are Game Objects.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 170.1
officialTextEn: Battlefields are Owned by a player.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 170.2
officialTextEn: Battlefields are not shuffled into Decks at the start of a game.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 170.2.a
officialTextEn: Battlefields are not played during the course of regular play.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 170.2.b
officialTextEn: Battlefields are established at the start of a game and remain in place for the duration of regular play.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 170.3
officialTextEn: Battlefields cannot be Killed during the course of regular play.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 170.4
officialTextEn: Battlefields cannot be Moved.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 170.5
officialTextEn: Battlefields are Locations.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 170.5.a
officialTextEn: Battlefields can be Origins of moves.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 170.5.b
officialTextEn: Battlefields can be Destinations of moves.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 170.6
officialTextEn: Any number of Units can be present at a Battlefield.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 170.7
officialTextEn: Battlefields can be targeted by spells or game effects.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 170.8
officialTextEn: Battlefields can have Passive Abilities. See rule 363. Passive Abilities for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 170.9
officialTextEn: Battlefields can have Triggered Abilities. See rule 382. Triggered Abilities for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 170.10
officialTextEn: Battlefields can have Activated Abilities. See rule 376. Activated Abilities for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 170.11
officialTextEn: Battlefields can be referenced in different states in card text:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 170.11.a
officialTextEn: Battlefields can be “occupied.” This means they have a Unit present.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 170.11.b
officialTextEn: Battlefields can be “uncontrolled.” This means no player controls them.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 170.11.c
officialTextEn: Battlefields can be “open.” This means they are unoccupied and uncontrolled.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 171
officialTextEn: Battlefields are not Permanents.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 172
officialTextEn: The number of Battlefields on the Board is determined by the Mode of Play.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 173
officialTextEn: Legends

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 174
officialTextEn: Legends are Game Objects.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 174.1
officialTextEn: Legends are Owned by a player.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 174.2
officialTextEn: Legends are not shuffled into Decks at the start of a game.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 174.2.a
officialTextEn: Legends are not played during the course of regular play.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 174.2.b
officialTextEn: Legends are established at the start of a game, and remain in place for the duration of regular play. Legends may be Created during the course of play. They will be Created ready unless the effect specifies otherwise.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 174.3
officialTextEn: Legends cannot be Killed during the course of regular play.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 174.4
officialTextEn: Legends cannot be Moved.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 174.5
officialTextEn: Legends can be targeted by spells or game effects.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 174.6
officialTextEn: Legends can have Passive Abilities. See rule 363. Passive Abilities for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 174.7
officialTextEn: Legends can have Triggered Abilities. See rule 382. Triggered Abilities for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 174.8
officialTextEn: Legends can have Activated Abilities. See rule 376. Activated Abilities for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 175
officialTextEn: Legends are not Permanents.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 176
officialTextEn: Legends may have one or more Domains.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 176.1
officialTextEn: The Champion Legend determines the Domain Identity of cards its owner can include. See rule 101. Deck Construction for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 177
officialTextEn: Multiple Types

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 178
officialTextEn: Game Objects can have multiple types.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 178.1
officialTextEn: A Game Object that is more than one type has the properties of all of their types, except where they are mutually exclusive.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 178.1.a
officialTextEn: Regardless of a Game Objects’ other types, there are some properties that are true of Game Objects of certain types. These properties take precedence when properties are mutually exclusive.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 178.1.a.1
officialTextEn: If a Game Object is a Unit, regardless of its other types, it has Might, can have damage marked on it, enters exhausted, and can be played to any valid location.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 178.1.a.1.a
officialTextEn: It will not be recalled to base from a Battlefield in step 5 of a cleanup.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 178.1.a.2
officialTextEn: If a Game Object is a Rune, regardless of its other types, it will be recycled to the Rune Deck.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 178.2
officialTextEn: A Game Object that is more than one type maintains all of the permissions of all types.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 178.2.a
officialTextEn: If a Game Object is a Unit, it has the standard move inherent ability.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 178.2.a.1
officialTextEn: It can move and become located at a Battlefield.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 178.3
officialTextEn: A Game Object that is more than one type can be affected by Game Effects that modify or interact with any of its types. Example: A unit that is also a gear can be affected by spells and abilities like the Ruination or Thermo Beam that say “Kill all units,” or “Kill all gear.” A unit that is also a gear can be targeted by spells and abilities like Vengeance or Rocket Barrage that say “Kill a unit,” or “Kill a gear.”

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 179
officialTextEn: Tokens

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 180
officialTextEn: Tokens are Game Objects created by spells and abilities during play.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 181
officialTextEn: Tokens can be represented by anything. Printed tokens are included in Riftbound booster packs, but they are not required to play a token.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 182
officialTextEn: A token's controller is the controller of the spell or ability that created it, unless the token's type innately determines control or that spell or ability specifies that a different player is the token's controller.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 183
officialTextEn: A token's owner is the player who controlled the effect that created it.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 184
officialTextEn: The effect that creates a token may specify the conditions or circumstances under which it enters the board. These stipulations may alter the usual steps for playing a card if the token is played.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 184.1
officialTextEn: The effect may state that the token enters ready or exhausted, if that state is contrary to the default for the token's type.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 184.2
officialTextEn: The effect may restrict the location to which the token may be played.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 184.3
officialTextEn: The effect may grant temporary abilities or modifications to the token.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 185
officialTextEn: Tokens are not cards.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 185.1
officialTextEn: “Token” is an intrinsic category of Game Objects, in the same way “card” is.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 185.1.a
officialTextEn: Token Game Objects cannot lose their token nature by any means.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 185.1.b
officialTextEn: Card Game Objects cannot become tokens by any means.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 185.2
officialTextEn: Tokens have some properties in common with cards.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 185.2.a
officialTextEn: Tokens can be played by their owner if their card type is played, following all the applicable steps for playing a card plus any restrictions or modifications from the effect that created the token. See rule 349. Playing Cards for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 185.2.b
officialTextEn: Token units have a Might.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 185.2.c
officialTextEn: Tokens may have one or more tags.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 185.2.d
officialTextEn: Tokens have a type. They follow all rules for their type unless otherwise specified. Example: A token unit is a unit. It enters exhausted, can take the standard move action, deals damage equal to its Might in combat, is destroyed if it takes damage equal to or greater than its might, can be chosen or otherwise affected by spells or abilities that choose or affect units, etc.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 185.2.e
officialTextEn: Tokens inherit the recycle destination of their type. Example: Token runes will be recycled to the Rune Deck. Token units, gear, and spells will be recycled to the Main Deck. Token battlefields and legends can’t be recycled.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 185.3
officialTextEn: Tokens differ from cards in some ways.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 185.3.a
officialTextEn: Tokens do not have costs.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 185.3.a.1
officialTextEn: Although tokens do not have costs, their cost is treated as being 0 for all purposes.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 185.3.a.2
officialTextEn: Tokens can have costs appended to them via applied Layer effects. Example: Deceiver’s conquer effect creates a 0 [M] Reflection unit token and applies a copy effect to that token. The copy effect will append all copyable traits, including the cost of the unit to be copied. This appends a cost to the Reflection token.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 185.3.b
officialTextEn: Tokens do not have domains.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 185.3.b.1
officialTextEn: Tokens can have domains appended to them via applied Layer effects. Example: A card reads in part “As you play this, pick a domain. All units and gear are that domain.” If that card is in play, any unit and gear tokens will have the chosen domain appended to them.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 186
officialTextEn: Tokens are Created on the board or the Chain and cannot exist elsewhere.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 186.1
officialTextEn: If a token is put into any Non-Board Zone besides the chain, it ceases to exist immediately after moving to its new zone.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 187
officialTextEn: The spell or ability that Creates a token specifies some of its characteristics. It may have other characteristics, as listed below.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 187.1
officialTextEn: A 1 [M] Recruit token is a domainless unit token with 1 Might and the Recruit tag.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 187.2
officialTextEn: A 3 [M] Sprite token with Temporary is a domainless unit token with 3 Might, the Fae tag, and the Temporary keyword. See rule 816. Temporary for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 187.3
officialTextEn: A 2 [M] Sand Soldier token is a domainless unit token with 2 Might and the Shurima tag.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 187.4
officialTextEn: A 3 [M] Mech token is a domainless unit token with 3 Might and the Mech tag.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 187.5
officialTextEn: A Gold gear token is a domainless gear token with “[Reaction][>] Kill this, [E]: [Add] [A].”

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 187.6
officialTextEn: A 0 [M] Reflection token is a domainless unit token with 0 Might.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 187.7
officialTextEn: A 1 [M] Bird token is a domainless unit token with 1 Might, the Bird tag, and the Deflect keyword. See rule 809. Deflect for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 187.8
officialTextEn: A Brush battlefield token is a domainless battlefield token with “Bird, Cat, Dog, Poro, and Ivern units here have +1 [M]” and “When you score here, you may replace this with the battlefield it replaced.”

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 187.9
officialTextEn: The Baron Pit battlefield token is a domainless battlefield token with “Units can move here from anywhere.”

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 187.10
officialTextEn: A 1 [M] Tentacle token is a domainless unit token with 1 Might and the Bilgewater tag.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 187.11
officialTextEn: A 0 [M] Shadow Clone token is a domainless unit token with 0 Might and “When I attack, you may banish a unit from your trash. If you do, give me [Assault 4] this turn.” See rule 807. Assault for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 187.12
officialTextEn: A Bomb gear token is a domainless gear token with “[Deploy]” and “[Deathknell][>] Deal 2 to an enemy unit here and kill all other Bombs you control here.” See rule 830. Deploy for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 188
officialTextEn: Control

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 189
officialTextEn: Control is the concept of a player having influence of a Game Object and applies differently to different card types.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 190
officialTextEn: Battlefields

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 190.1
officialTextEn: Control is established over Battlefields through the course of play.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 190.2
officialTextEn: Control is a binary state for Battlefields and an Identifier for players.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 190.2.a
officialTextEn: A Battlefield is Controlled or Uncontrolled.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 190.2.b
officialTextEn: A Battlefield is Controlled by a specific player or Controlled by no one.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 190.3
officialTextEn: Control can be Contested through the course of play.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 190.3.a
officialTextEn: Contested is a temporary status applied to a Battlefield when a Unit controlled by a Player who does not currently Control that Battlefield Moves or otherwise becomes present there.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 190.3.a.1
officialTextEn: Units moving to or being played to a battlefield apply Contested status if that Battlefield is not already Contested and that Unit’s controller does not already control that battlefield.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 190.3.a.2
officialTextEn: A Unit changing controller while located at a Battlefield will also apply Contested status to that Battlefield if it isn’t Contested and if the new controller doesn’t control that Battlefield.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 190.3.b
officialTextEn: Once a Showdown or Combat begins at a Battlefield, it remains Contested until Control is established or re-established.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 190.3.b.1
officialTextEn: If a player who applied Contested status to a Battlefield controls no Units there and there is no ongoing Showdown or Combat at that Battlefield, then Contested status is removed in the following Cleanup.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 190.3.c
officialTextEn: The state of a Battlefield being Contested is used to determine when Combat should occur and when a Non-Combat Showdown should occur.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 190.3.d
officialTextEn: At this time Game Effects cannot reference this status.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 190.4
officialTextEn: Control is established by having Units at a Battlefield at the end of a Showdown or Combat after applying the contested status.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 190.4.a
officialTextEn: If a player controls Units at a Battlefield, outside of Combat, they maintain Control of that Battlefield for as long as they have Units at that Battlefield.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 190.4.b
officialTextEn: While a Combat or Showdown is ongoing at a Battlefield, Control of that Battlefield cannot change until instructed by steps of the Combat or Showdown.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 190.4.c
officialTextEn: If a player has no Units at a Battlefield and the turn is in an Open state, they lose Control of that Battlefield in the following cleanup unless there is a Combat or Showdown ongoing there.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 190.5
officialTextEn: Control is a constant state.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 190.6
officialTextEn: Control of a Battlefield determines Control of its Abilities.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 190.6.a
officialTextEn: While a Battlefield is Controlled, its Controller controls its Abilities unless that ability indicates another player does. The controlling player takes responsibility for adding them to the Chain if applicable, and makes all choices required by them unless otherwise specified.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 190.6.b
officialTextEn: While a Battlefield is Uncontrolled, its Abilities are also Uncontrolled unless that ability indicates a player controls it. If there is no such indication, the Turn Player takes responsibility for adding them to the Chain if applicable, makes all choices required by them unless otherwise specified, and is treated as their Controller if any game rule or effect requires one. Example: The Arena’s Greatest is a battlefield that reads “At the start of each player's first Beginning Phase, that player gains 1 point.” This ability will usually trigger while the battlefield has no controller. If it does, the Turn Player goes through the steps of adding the ability to the chain and receives priority after doing so, exactly as if they controlled the ability.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 190.6.c
officialTextEn: If an Ability of a Battlefield indicates that a specific player makes a choice, that player is the Ability’s controller. They take responsibility for adding it to the chain if applicable and make all choices required by the ability. They and only they control the ability, regardless of who controls the Battlefield. Example: Abandoned Hall is a battlefield that reads “When a player plays a spell, they may give a unit they control here +1 might this turn.” The ability indicates that the player who played the spell makes the choice, so that player takes responsibility for putting the ability on the chain and makes all choices. They control the triggered ability.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 190.6.d
officialTextEn: “You” in a battlefield’s abilities refers to the battlefield’s Controller, as does the implied “you” in instructions that don’t specify a player like “draw 1.” If the battlefield has no Controller, “you” refers to no one, and all such instructions are ignored.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 191
officialTextEn: Everything Else

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 191.1
officialTextEn: Players control their own Champion Legend.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 191.2
officialTextEn: When a player Plays, Hides, or Creates a Card or other Game Object, they are established as that Game Object's Controller.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 191.3
officialTextEn: For Spells, they are the Spell's Controller.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 191.3.a
officialTextEn: That player chooses targets.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 191.3.b
officialTextEn: That player chooses modes.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 191.3.c
officialTextEn: That player pays costs.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 191.4
officialTextEn: For Permanents and Runes, when they Enter the Board, that player is assigned as that Game Object's Controller.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 191.4.a
officialTextEn: That player may make decisions about the Game Object's Inherent Abilities.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 191.4.b
officialTextEn: That player may make decisions about the Game Object's Unique Abilities.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 191.4.c
officialTextEn: That player may make decisions about any game effects or decisions necessary while the card is being played.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 191.4.d
officialTextEn: That player may make decisions about any game effects created from "When you play me" effects of Permanents.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 191.5
officialTextEn: For Abilities, they are the Ability’s Controller.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 191.5.a
officialTextEn: By default, the Controller of an Ability’s Source is the Controller of that Ability.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 191.5.a.1
officialTextEn: If an Ability’s Source is located in a non-Board Zone, the Ability’s Controller is the Owner of the Source.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 191.5.a.2
officialTextEn: If an Ability allows players other than the Controller or Owner of its Source to play it, the player that plays the Ability Controls the Ability.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 191.5.b
officialTextEn: Changes to Control of an Ability’s Source do not change Control of that Ability.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 191.5.c
officialTextEn: That player chooses targets.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 191.5.d
officialTextEn: That player chooses modes.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 191.5.e
officialTextEn: That player pays costs.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 192
officialTextEn: When a game effect or rules text refers to the Controller of a specific object, it can be referring to either context interchangeably.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 192.1
officialTextEn: The method of assignment of control is different, but the status of Control is the same across all Game Objects.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 193
officialTextEn: Winning

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 194
officialTextEn: Players win Riftbound games primarily through gaining points.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 194.1
officialTextEn: Players can gain points a number of ways:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 194.1.a
officialTextEn: Holding a Battlefield. See rule 469. Scoring for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 194.1.b
officialTextEn: Conquering a Battlefield. See rule 469. Scoring for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 194.1.c
officialTextEn: Spells, Triggered Abilities and Activated Abilities that instruct them to gain one or more points.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 194.1.d
officialTextEn: When an opponent Burns Out and picks that player to gain 1 point. See rule 432. Burn Out for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 194.2
officialTextEn: A player wins the game if, in a cleanup, they have points greater than or equal to the Victory Score and more points than any other player. See rule 318. Cleanups for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 194.2.a
officialTextEn: If more than one player has points greater than or equal to the Victory Score, whichever player has more points wins.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 194.2.b
officialTextEn: If those players have the same number of points, play continues until one player has more points in a cleanup.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 194.3
officialTextEn: The Victory Score is 8 points by default.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 194.3.a
officialTextEn: Some game modes or card effects may alter the Victory Score. See rule 483. Modes of Play for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 194.4
officialTextEn: Players cannot have less than 0 points.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 194.4.a
officialTextEn: If a player would lose 1 or more points while they have 0 points, nothing occurs.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 194.4.b
officialTextEn: Any effects that trigger on a player losing points do not trigger.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 195
officialTextEn: A player also wins the game if an effect instructs them to do so, or if they are the only player remaining in the game.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 195.1
officialTextEn: If an effect instructs a player to lose the game, that player is immediately removed from the game. See rule 649. Conceding for more information about being removed from the game.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 196
officialTextEn: When a player wins the game, the game ends.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 197
officialTextEn: Locations

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 198
officialTextEn: Locations are the Game Objects and Zones where permanents and runes may be located.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 198.1
officialTextEn: Locations include the Battlefields and the Bases.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 198.2
officialTextEn: A permanent’s Location is a characteristic of that permanent that may be referenced by Game Effects.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 199
officialTextEn: A Game Object that comprises a Location is also a Game Object at that location.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 199.1
officialTextEn: A Battlefield is both a location and also a Game Object at that location.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 200
officialTextEn: Locations can be Destinations and Origins for movement. See rule 447. Movement for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 201
officialTextEn: Costs

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 202
officialTextEn: Some Game Effects will instruct players to pay resources, spend counters or XP, or perform game actions as a Cost in order to perform a linked Effect.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 203
officialTextEn: Costs must be paid in order to get their linked Effect.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 203.1
officialTextEn: Paying a Cost requires a player to perform the appropriate game action: pay resources, spend counters or XP, kill units, etc.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 203.2
officialTextEn: The Cost is still considered paid even if the associated game action is replaced.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 203.3
officialTextEn: If the game action associated with a Cost is impossible for any reason such that a player cannot perform it, then they cannot pay the Cost and they will not execute the linked Effect.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 204
officialTextEn: Costs paid in this way might be:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 204.1
officialTextEn: Base Costs: These costs are the most fundamental costs that must be paid to finalize a card or ability.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 204.1.a
officialTextEn: On cards, the Base Cost is found in the upper left corner of the card.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 204.1.b
officialTextEn: On activated abilities, the Base Cost is the resource or instruction written before the “:”. If there are multiple choices for costs to pay for an activated ability before the “:”, the Base Cost is whatever cost the player chooses from among those options. Example: Legion Marauder is a unit that reads in part “[Empower] — [1] or [C].” This is functionally short for “[1] or [C]: Empower me. Play only if not empowered.” When finalizing the ability to the chain, the controller of the chain item will choose one of the base costs to pay. That is the base cost of the ability.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 204.1.c
officialTextEn: On Triggered Abilities, the Base Cost if it is present is the Costs within Instructions that appears as the first part of the effect. It must be paid to finalize the triggered ability. See rule 204.3. Costs within Instructions for more information. Example: Overzealous Fan is a unit that reads “When I defend, you may kill me to move an attacking unit to its base.” In order to finalize the ability to the chain, its controller must kill Overzealous Fan.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 204.2
officialTextEn: Additional Costs: These Costs are in addition to the base cost of the card or ability and will include “as an additional cost.”

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 204.2.a
officialTextEn: Additional Costs must be paid to finalize the card or ability, in addition to the base cost.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 204.3
officialTextEn: Costs within Instructions: These Costs are part of the resolution of a spell or ability, and will take the form “[do X] to [do Y].”

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 204.3.a
officialTextEn: When Costs within Instructions appear in spells, activated abilities, or in later parts of triggered abilities, the cost must be paid to get the effect during resolution of the spell or ability. Example: Bullet Time is a spell that reads “Pay any amount of [A] to deal that much damage to all enemy units at a battlefield.” As the spell resolves, its controller pays any amount of [A] as a cost, and deals that much damage to all units at a battlefield as the effect. Example: Ancient Henge is a gear that reads “[Reaction][>] [E]: Pay any amount of Energy to Add that much [A].” As the ability resolves, its controller pays any amount of Energy as a cost, and Adds that much [A] as the effect. Example: Insightful Investigator is a unit that reads “When you play me, choose an opponent. They reveal their hand. You may pay 2 XP to choose a card from their hand. If you do, they discard that card and draw 1.” As the ability resolves, its controller may pay 2 XP as a cost, and chooses a card from that player’s hand as the effect.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 204.4
officialTextEn: Applied Costs: These Costs are applied to one or more Game Actions, and typically take the form of a passive ability with a Cost within Instructions preceded by “must.” Example: Mageseeker Investigator reads in part “Opponents must pay [A] for each unit beyond the first to move multiple units to my battlefield at the same time.” This is an applied cost.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 204.4.a
officialTextEn: The associated Game Action is the linked Effect for the Cost.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 204.4.b
officialTextEn: Applied Costs are paid as the Game Action is performed. They do not use the chain and cannot be reacted to.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 204.4.b.1
officialTextEn: Abilities that Add resources with the Reaction keyword can be activated at any time when costs need to be paid. See rule 430. Add for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 204.4.c
officialTextEn: If a player can’t pay or chooses not to pay the Applied Cost, they cannot perform the associated Game Action.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 205
officialTextEn: An instruction that requires a player to pay resources or spend counters or XP that does not also have a linked Effect, is not a Cost. Example: A card effect reads, “When I attack, you may pay [4][C]. If you do, kill a unit here.” Paying [4][C] in this way is not a cost of the ability, base or otherwise, but a game action being performed by a player. The later instruction checks whether the game action was performed, not whether a cost was paid—if paying [4][C] was replaced for any reason, the later linked instruction will not execute.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 206
officialTextEn: Effects that need to determine a card or token’s cost for any purpose always use its printed—or if a copy effect is applied, copied—cost, even if that cost is increased, decreased, or ignored as the card is played. Example: Sky Splitter is a spell that costs [8] and says in part “This spell's Energy cost is reduced by the highest Might among units you control.” Lux, Illuminated is a unit that says “When you play a spell that costs 5 or more, give me +3 [M] this turn.” If a player who controls Lux plays Sky Splitter, Lux’s ability will trigger, regardless of how much was actually paid for Sky Splitter. Example: Defy is a spell which reads “Counter a spell that costs no more than [4] and no more than [A].” Rocket Barrage is a spell that costs [4][C] and has a Repeat cost of [4][C]. Rocket Barrage is a legal target for Defy even if Rocket Barrage’s Repeat cost is paid, because Defy only checks the printed or copied cost of its target. Example: Atakhan is a unit that reads in part “You may kill a friendly unit as an additional cost to play me. If you do, I cost [1] less for each Energy it costs and [Y] less for each Power it costs.” If a player plays Atakhan and chooses to kill a Reflection token that is currently a copy of Noxus Hopeful, Atakhan will cost [4] less.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 206.1
officialTextEn: Effects that need to determine an ability’s cost for any purpose use its base cost, ignoring any alterations to that base cost unless otherwise specified. Example: A card reads “When you play an activated ability with Energy cost [7] or more, you may exhaust me to ready up to 2 runes.” A gear has an activated ability that reads “[12], Banish this: Choose an opponent. Banish all units they control. This ability costs [1] less for each point the chosen opponent has.” The ability of the first card will trigger when the activated ability is played, even if the chosen opponent has 6 or more points. Example: An equipment has an ability that reads “Equip [4][A]. This ability costs [1] less for each occupied enemy battlefield.” If its controller plays a unit with Weaponmaster, the Weaponmaster trigger will refer to the cost including the alterations. This is because Weaponmaster specifies that it includes modifications to the cost.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 300
officialTextEn: Playing the Game

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 301
officialTextEn: The Turn

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 302
officialTextEn: Play continues cyclically until one player wins.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 303
officialTextEn: The phases of a turn are rigid, but the actions taken during those steps can be done in any order, unless otherwise specified.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 303.1
officialTextEn: Game Actions of any nature are performed one at a time and are executed completely.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 303.2
officialTextEn: Game Actions cannot be performed simultaneously for any reason.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 303.2.a
officialTextEn: If one or more game actions, game effects, or Triggered Abilities are activated simultaneously, then Turn Order is referenced to organize the sequence of actions, starting with the current Turn Player. See rule 382. Triggered Abilities for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 304
officialTextEn: The Turn Player is the player taking the current turn.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 305
officialTextEn: When there are no items on the Chain and the Turn Player cannot or chooses not to perform any Discretionary Actions, the current phase or step of the turn ends and the next phase, step, or turn begins.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 306
officialTextEn: The Turn Player changes when the current Turn Player reaches the End of all of the Phases of their Turn.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 307
officialTextEn: States of the Turn

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 308
officialTextEn: At any given time, the turn is in either a Neutral State or a Showdown State.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 308.1
officialTextEn: If a Showdown or Combat is in progress, the turn is in a Showdown State.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 308.1.a
officialTextEn: Only cards and abilities with the Action or Reaction keywords can be played or activated in a Showdown State.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 308.2
officialTextEn: If no Showdown or Combat is in progress, the turn is in a Neutral State.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 309
officialTextEn: At any given time, the turn is in either an Open State or a Closed State.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 309.1
officialTextEn: If a Chain exists, the turn is in a Closed State.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 309.1.a
officialTextEn: Only cards and abilities with the Reaction keyword can be played or activated in a Closed State.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 309.2
officialTextEn: If no Chain exists, the turn is in an Open State.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 310
officialTextEn: These descriptions can be combined, such that the turn is always in one of these four states:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 310.1
officialTextEn: Neutral Open: There is no Showdown or Combat in progress and no Chain exists.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 310.1.a
officialTextEn: By default, cards can be played and abilities activated only when a player has priority on their turn in a Neutral Open state.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 310.2
officialTextEn: Neutral Closed: There is no Showdown or Combat in progress and a Chain exists.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 310.3
officialTextEn: Showdown Open: A Showdown or Combat is in progress and no Chain exists.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 310.4
officialTextEn: Showdown Closed: A Showdown or Combat is in progress and a Chain exists.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 311
officialTextEn: Priority and Focus

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 312
officialTextEn: At any given time, up to one player has Priority.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 312.1
officialTextEn: Priority is the singular exclusive right to take Discretionary Actions. See rule 411.1. Discretionary Actions for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 312.1.a
officialTextEn: The player with Priority can take appropriately timed Discretionary Actions.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 312.1.b
officialTextEn: If no player has Priority, no player can take Discretionary Actions.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 312.1.b.1
officialTextEn: Players can always take and make choices for Limited Actions when instructed, regardless of Priority.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 312.2
officialTextEn: A player receives Priority at the following times:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 312.2.a
officialTextEn: When the turn is in a Neutral Open State during their Main Phase.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 312.2.b
officialTextEn: When the turn is in a Showdown State and they gain Focus.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 312.2.c
officialTextEn: When the turn is in a Closed State, all pending chain items finish being finalized, and they control the next item on the Chain.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 312.2.d
officialTextEn: When the turn is in a Closed State, they are the next Player in Turn Order, and the player with Priority passes.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 312.3
officialTextEn: When a player is granted Priority, it is either created if no player has it or taken from the player with Priority.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 313
officialTextEn: At any given time, up to one player has Focus.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 313.1
officialTextEn: Focus is the permission to take appropriately timed Discretionary Actions when the turn is in a Showdown Open State. See rule 307. States of the Turn for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 313.1.a
officialTextEn: The player with Focus must obey any additional restrictions on which Discretionary Actions may be performed. Example: A player with Focus may not play spells or activate abilities that don't have the Action or Reaction keywords.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 313.2
officialTextEn: A player who gains Focus also gains Priority.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 313.3
officialTextEn: A player who passes Priority retains Focus.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 313.4
officialTextEn: A player may not make discretionary actions with Focus unless they also possess Priority.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 313.5
officialTextEn: If the turn is in a Neutral State, no player has Focus.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 314
officialTextEn: Phases of the Turn

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 315
officialTextEn: Start of Turn

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 315.1
officialTextEn: Awaken Phase

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 315.1.a
officialTextEn: The following Task becomes Outstanding:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 315.1.b
officialTextEn: 1. The Turn Player readies all Game Objects they control that are able to be readied. See rule 416. Ready for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 315.2
officialTextEn: Beginning Phase

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 315.2.a
officialTextEn: Beginning Step

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 315.2.a.1
officialTextEn: At the start of Beginning Phase game effects take place.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 315.2.b
officialTextEn: Scoring Step

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 315.2.b.1
officialTextEn: The following Task becomes Outstanding:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 315.2.b.2
officialTextEn: 1. The Turn Player Holds all Battlefields they Control. See rule 469. Scoring for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 315.2.b.3
officialTextEn: Reminder: In Modes of Play with Teams, Battlefields controlled by a Teammate of the Turn Player during this step are disqualified from being scored this turn by that team.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 315.3
officialTextEn: Channel Phase

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 315.3.a
officialTextEn: The following Task becomes Outstanding:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 315.3.b
officialTextEn: 1. The Turn Player channels 2 runes from their Rune Deck. See rule 431. Channel for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 315.3.b.1
officialTextEn: If there are fewer than 2 runes in the Rune Deck, they channel as many as possible.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 315.4
officialTextEn: Draw Phase

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 315.4.a
officialTextEn: The following Task becomes Outstanding:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 315.4.b
officialTextEn: 1. The Turn Player draws 1.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 315.4.b.1
officialTextEn: If there are no cards remaining in their Main Deck to draw, the Turn Player has been Burned Out. See rule 432. Burn Out for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 315.4.b.2
officialTextEn: After completing the Burn Out the Turn Player still Draws 1.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316
officialTextEn: Main Phase

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316.1
officialTextEn: When all steps of the Start of Turn have been completed, the Main Phase begins.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316.2
officialTextEn: The following Tasks become Outstanding in the specified order:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316.3
officialTextEn: 1. Each player's Rune Pool empties. Any unspent Energy and Power are lost. See rule 165. Rune Pools for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316.4
officialTextEn: 2. At the start of Main Phase game effects take place.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316.5
officialTextEn: The Main Phase has no defined structure.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316.5.a
officialTextEn: A player may take any number of Discretionary Actions they are able to perform during this phase. See rule 411.1. Discretionary Actions for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316.5.b
officialTextEn: This is denoted as a Neutral Open State, and only the Turn Player has the ability to play spells or activate abilities. See rule 307. States of the Turn for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316.5.b.1
officialTextEn: In Modes of Play with teammates, the Turn Player's teammates may play spells and activate abilities, including ones without Action or Reaction. They can only do so when the Turn Player invites them to do so with their own Priority.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316.6
officialTextEn: As a result of a player taking Discretionary Actions, one or more structured phases may occur.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316.7
officialTextEn: Combat

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316.7.a
officialTextEn: A Combat occurs as a result of Units controlled by opposing players being present at the same Battlefield.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316.7.b
officialTextEn: This could be the result of a Standard Move Intrinsic Ability, a Spell, or other Game Effect.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316.7.c
officialTextEn: The source effect does not change the structure or flow of Combat once initiated.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316.7.d
officialTextEn: A Combat can only occur between two players. See rule 461. Combat for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316.7.e
officialTextEn: Play proceeds following the steps of combat. See rule 465. The Steps of Combat for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316.7.f
officialTextEn: Combat will also include a Showdown.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316.8
officialTextEn: Showdowns

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316.8.a
officialTextEn: A Showdown occurs when a Combat occurs.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316.8.a.1
officialTextEn: Showdowns that occur as a result of Combat are a Sub-Phase of Combat.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316.8.b
officialTextEn: A Showdown is marked as Staged at a Battlefield in the cleanup after the Contested status is applied to that Battlefield.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316.8.b.1
officialTextEn: Showdowns that occur as a result of a player moving to an empty Battlefield are a stand-alone Phase and do not create a Combat.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316.8.b.1.a
officialTextEn: These Showdowns are called Non-Combat Showdowns. During the proceedings of a Non-Combat Showdown, units controlled by a different player may become present at the Battlefield where the Showdown is ongoing. This will cause the Showdown to become a Combat Showdown in the following cleanup.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316.8.c
officialTextEn: A Showdown is a structured Window of Opportunity where Players may play cards and activate abilities with Action or Reaction. See rule 341. Showdowns for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316.9
officialTextEn: When a player has no more Discretionary Actions they wish to execute, they must indicate they are ending their turn.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316.9.a
officialTextEn: This ends the Main Phase.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 316.9.b
officialTextEn: Play proceeds to the Ending Phase.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 317
officialTextEn: Ending Phase

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 317.1
officialTextEn: Ending Step

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 317.1.a
officialTextEn: At the end of this turn and at the end of turn Game Effects take place.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 317.1.b
officialTextEn: Specific game effects and abilities will reference this timing and phase as necessary.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 317.2
officialTextEn: Expiration Step

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 317.2.a
officialTextEn: Invoke an Ending Special Cleanup. See rule 318. Cleanups for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 317.2.b
officialTextEn: Insert “3c. Heal all Units.”

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 317.2.c
officialTextEn: Insert “3d. All ‘this turn’ effects expire simultaneously.”

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 317.2.d
officialTextEn: Insert “3e. Each player’s Rune Pool empties. Any unspent Energy and Power are lost.”

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 317.2.e
officialTextEn: The following Task becomes Outstanding:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 317.2.f
officialTextEn: 1. If any items underwent the FEPR process, return to the start of the Expiration Step

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 317.3
officialTextEn: The next player with their Turn queued becomes the Turn Player.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 318
officialTextEn: Cleanups

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 319
officialTextEn: A Cleanup will be made an Outstanding Task at the following times:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 319.1
officialTextEn: After the game transitions to or from an Open or Closed state

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 319.2
officialTextEn: After the game transitions between Phases, unless specified otherwise

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 319.3
officialTextEn: After a Pending Item is added to the Chain

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 319.4
officialTextEn: After a Pending Item becomes a Finalized Item on the Chain

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 319.5
officialTextEn: After a Chain Item is removed from the Chain for any reason

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 319.6
officialTextEn: After any number of Game Objects enter or leave the Board

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 319.7
officialTextEn: After the status of any number of Game Objects changes for any reason

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 319.8
officialTextEn: After a Move is completed

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 320
officialTextEn: While a Cleanup is occurring, Chain Items cannot be Finalized or Resolved.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 320.1
officialTextEn: New Pending Items can be added, but Finalized Items cannot be executed and Priority and Focus are not passed or awarded.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 321
officialTextEn: Similarly, while Chain Items are Resolving, a Cleanup cannot occur.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 321.1
