officialTextEn: If an event occurs during the Resolution of a Chain Item that qualifies for a Cleanup, that Cleanup will be made an Outstanding Task.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 322
officialTextEn: If an event occurs during a Cleanup that qualifies for a Cleanup, another Cleanup will occur immediately after the first completes, repeating until a Cleanup occurs with no new change in the game’s state.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 322.1
officialTextEn: These new Cleanups are themselves Outstanding Tasks.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 323
officialTextEn: When a Cleanup occurs, the following Tasks become Outstanding in the order described:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 323.1
officialTextEn: 1. If a player has points greater than or equal to the Victory Score, and more points than every opponent, that player wins.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 323.2
officialTextEn: 2. Assign or Remove the Attacker or Defender designation from Units as needed if there is a Combat in progress

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 323.2.a
officialTextEn: If there are Units present at the Battlefield the Combat is taking place at, but do not have a designation, they gain the same designation as their Controller now

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 323.2.b
officialTextEn: If there are Units present at the Battlefield the Combat is taking place at, but have the opposite designation of their controller, they lose that designation, and gain the same designation as their controller now

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 323.2.c
officialTextEn: If there are Units at locations other than the Battlefield that the Combat is taking place at, but have either Attacker or Defender designations, they lose those designations now

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 323.3
officialTextEn: 3. Handle outstanding board state

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 323.4
officialTextEn: 3a. All Units that have Lethal Damage marked on them are killed and placed in their owners' Trash. See rule 142.4. For more information on lethal damage.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 323.5
officialTextEn: 4. Players lose control of any controlled Battlefields without their Units occupying them if the turn is in an Open State and there is no Showdown or Combat ongoing there.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 323.6
officialTextEn: 5. Recall all of the following Game Objects, unless an effect would indicate otherwise: Unattached non-Unit Gear located at Battlefields Non-Unit Runes located at Battlefields Unattached Permanents and Runes in Bases other than their controller’s

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 323.6.a
officialTextEn: Remove all Hidden cards from all Battlefields that are not controlled by the same player and place them in their owner's Trash.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 323.7
officialTextEn: 6. Mark a Showdown as Staged at each Battlefield that Contested was applied to and that has no ongoing Combat.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 323.7.a
officialTextEn: The Showdown remains Staged at that Battlefield as long as it is Contested and has units present controlled by the player that applied Contested.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 323.8
officialTextEn: 7. Mark a Combat as Staged at each Battlefield that Contested was applied to that have Units present controlled by opposing players, and that has no ongoing Combat.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 323.9
officialTextEn: 7a. If Units of two opposing players are no longer present at a Battlefield that has a Combat Staged before it has opened, the Combat will cease being Staged

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 323.10
officialTextEn: 8. Remove Contested status from each Battlefield without Units controlled by the player who applied Contested to that Battlefield and without a Showdown or Combat ongoing there.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 323.10.a
officialTextEn: If as a result of the removal of Contested status there are Units located at an uncontested Battlefield that their controller does not control, their controller applies Contested status to that Battlefield.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 323.11
officialTextEn: 9. If the current state is a Neutral Open State and one or more Showdowns are Staged at Battlefields without a Combat staged, the Turn Player chooses one of those Battlefields. A Showdown begins there.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 323.12
officialTextEn: 10. If the current state is a Neutral Open State and one or more Combats are Staged at Battlefields, the Turn Player chooses one of those Battlefields. Combat begins there.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 323.13
officialTextEn: 10a. If the current state is Showdown Open State and Combat is Staged at a Battlefield where there is a Non-Combat Showdown ongoing, that Showdown becomes a Combat Showdown.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 324
officialTextEn: Special Cleanups are Cleanup steps invoked at specific times that have additional steps not present in a normal Cleanup.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 324.1
officialTextEn: When a Special Cleanup is invoked, the unique steps added will be inserted and defined by the sub- section that invokes it. Example: When a Combat Cleanup is invoked, the Combat section defines what steps are added to the Cleanup. See rule 468. The Resolution Step for more information. Example: When an End of Turn Cleanup is invoked, the End of Turn Phase subsection defines what steps are added to the Cleanup. See rule 317. The Ending Phase for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 324.2
officialTextEn: If events during a Special Cleanup require another Cleanup, a normal Cleanup is invoked, not another iteration of the Special Cleanup.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 325
officialTextEn: Chains and Showdowns

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 326
officialTextEn: Players can act during the following Windows of Opportunity that occur during the course of regular play:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 326.1
officialTextEn: During a Chain

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 326.2
officialTextEn: During a Showdown

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 327
officialTextEn: Chains

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 328
officialTextEn: The Chain is a Non-Board Zone that temporarily exists whenever a card or ability is played.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 328.1
officialTextEn: Cards, abilities, and tokens are placed here as part of the process of being played. See rule 349. The Process of Play for more information. See rule 360. Abilities for more information on Abilities.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 329
officialTextEn: Cards, tokens, and abilities added to the chain are added as Pending Chain Items that become Finalized Chain Items.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 329.1
officialTextEn: Pending Items are on the Chain.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 329.2
officialTextEn: Chain Items are Pending until the “Check Legality” step of playing a card. See rule 349. Playing Cards for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 329.3
officialTextEn: When a Pending Chain Item is no longer Pending it is finalized and becomes a Finalized Chain Item.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 330
officialTextEn: The Chain exists as long as a Chain Item is on it.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 330.1
officialTextEn: Only one Chain can exist at a time.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 330.2
officialTextEn: If a card, token, or ability would begin to be played while a Chain already exists, it is placed on the existing Chain.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 331
officialTextEn: The State of the Turn is partially determined by whether or not the Chain currently exists.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 331.1
officialTextEn: The turn is said to be in a Closed State if a Chain exists.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 331.1.a
officialTextEn: Cards of all Categories, by default, cannot be played during a Closed State.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 331.1.b
officialTextEn: Card abilities, by default, cannot be played during a Closed State.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 331.2
officialTextEn: The turn is said to be in an Open State if no Chain exists.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 332
officialTextEn: Handling Tasks and Resolving Chain Items

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 333
officialTextEn: A Task is one or more steps or processes that one or more Players must perform before continuing with any other actions.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 333.1
officialTextEn: Tasks include, but are not limited to: Cleanups, the actions performed during the Start of Turn Process, throughout Combat in its various steps, and the actions performed during the End of Turn Process. See rule 318. Cleanups for more information on Cleanups See rule 315. Start of Turn for more information on the Start of Turn process See rule 461. Combat for more information on the steps of Combat See rule 317. Ending Phase for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 334
officialTextEn: Whenever a Player takes one or more actions that incur Tasks they should refer to the process of HOT FEPR: Handle Outstanding Tasks; then Finalize, Execute, Pass, Resolve.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 334.1
officialTextEn: In the course of Handling Outstanding Tasks, Chain Items may be added to the Chain. They will remain there until the Tasks are complete.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 334.2
officialTextEn: When all Outstanding Tasks are completed, all pending Chain Items will subsequently be processed by the FEPR process.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 334.2.a
officialTextEn: During the FEPR process, new Tasks may be incurred. Complete the current step of the process and then pause and complete the necessary Tasks before continuing.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 335
officialTextEn: If there are no Outstanding Tasks, no pending Chain Items, no ongoing Showdown or Combat, and it is the Main Phase, the Turn Player receives priority. If there are no Outstanding Tasks, no pending Chain Items, no ongoing Showdown, and it is any other phase of the turn, proceed to the next substep, step, phase, or turn.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 335.1
officialTextEn: If there are no Outstanding Tasks, no pending Chain Items, and there is an ongoing Showdown, the player with Focus receives priority.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 336
officialTextEn: When there are no outstanding Tasks and there are pending Chain Items on the Chain, players should refer to the FEPR process to proceed.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 336.1
officialTextEn: In the sequence of resolving FEPR more Chain Items may become Pending Chain Items. These will be processed by the same FEPR process that produced them.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 337
officialTextEn: Step 1: Finalize

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 337.1
officialTextEn: If there is at least one Chain Item Pending, the controller of the oldest Pending Chain Item must complete the steps of Playing that Pending Item until it is a Finalized Item or leaves the Chain. See rule 349. Playing Cards for more information on finalizing chain items.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 337.1.a
officialTextEn: Finalizing an item to the chain does not pass Priority.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 337.1.b
officialTextEn: Chain Items are Finalized in the order they were appended to the Chain.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 337.2
officialTextEn: If, after finalizing the Chain Item, that item is a Unit, Gear, or an ability that Adds resources, it resolves immediately—Move to Step 4: Resolve. See rule 349. Playing Cards for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 337.3
officialTextEn: If, after finalizing the Chain Item, there are still Pending Chain Items, return to Step 1. Finalize.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 337.4
officialTextEn: If, after finalizing the Chain Item, there are no more items on the chain to be Finalized, the controller of the next item on the chain gains Priority. Move to Step 2: Execute.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 338
officialTextEn: Step 2: Execute

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 338.1
officialTextEn: The player with Priority may do any the following:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 338.1.a
officialTextEn: Play a Card or Activated Ability that is legally timed.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 338.1.a.1
officialTextEn: Cards and Activated Abilities, by default, cannot be played during a Closed State.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 338.1.a.2
officialTextEn: A Legally Timed Card or Activated Ability would be one with Reaction or one that will have Reaction when played under appropriate circumstances.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 338.1.a.3
officialTextEn: Other exceptions may be created during regular play.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 338.1.a.4
officialTextEn: The Card or Activated Ability will be added to the chain as a Pending Item, following the steps of playing a card.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 338.1.a.5
officialTextEn: This can be an additional item to the item that Started the Chain in the case of the first player with Priority after creating the Chain.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 338.1.a.6
officialTextEn: Whether a Card or Activated Ability is legally timed is evaluated during the “Check Legality” step of Playing a Card. See rule 349. Playing Cards for more information. See rule 399. Playing or Activating Abilities for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 338.1.a.7
officialTextEn: Playing a Card or Activated Ability will create one or more Pending Items. Return to Step 1: Finalize.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 338.1.b
officialTextEn: Pass Priority

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 338.1.b.1
officialTextEn: The player with Priority passes Priority to the next Player in Turn Order. Proceed to Step 3: Pass.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 339
officialTextEn: Step 3: Pass

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 339.1
officialTextEn: If all players have passed Priority in sequence without adding any items to the Chain, proceed to Step 4: Resolve.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 339.2
officialTextEn: Otherwise, the player with Priority passes Priority to the next Player in Turn Order. Return to Step 2: Execute.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 340
officialTextEn: Step 4: Resolve

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 340.1
officialTextEn: The newest Finalized Chain Item resolves. Execute its game effects in their entirety. See rule 349. Playing Cards for more information on resolving spells. See rule 399. Playing or Activating Abilities for more information on resolving abilities.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 340.2
officialTextEn: If the Chain is empty, play proceeds in an Open State.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 340.2.a
officialTextEn: If this occurs during a Showdown and the chain wasn’t initiated by a triggered ability or an ability that Adds resources, focus passes to the next player in turn order.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 340.3
officialTextEn: If the Chain is not empty and there are one or more Pending Items, return to Step 1: Finalize.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 340.4
officialTextEn: If the Chain is not empty and there are no Pending Items, the controller of the newest item on the chain gains Priority. Return to Step 2: Execute.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 341
officialTextEn: Showdowns

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 342
officialTextEn: A Showdown is a Window of Opportunity in which Players have an Open State in which they may play Spells in an alternating fashion.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 342.1
officialTextEn: Each spell played this way creates a Chain as normal.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 343
officialTextEn: The State of the turn is partially determined by whether or not a Showdown or Combat is in progress.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 343.1
officialTextEn: The turn is said to be in a Showdown State if a Showdown or Combat is in progress.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 343.1.a
officialTextEn: Cards of all Categories, by default, cannot be played during a Showdown State.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 343.1.b
officialTextEn: Card abilities, by default, cannot be played during a Showdown State.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 343.2
officialTextEn: The turn is said to be in a Neutral State if no Showdown or Combat is in progress.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 344
officialTextEn: A Showdown begins when Control of a Battlefield is Contested during a Cleanup and the turn is in a Neutral Open State.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 344.1
officialTextEn: If Control of a Battlefield is Contested between two players, then a Showdown will be opened as the first step of Combat. If a Showdown is already ongoing at that Battlefield, it will become a Combat Showdown and a Combat will initiate there. See rule 461. Combat for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 344.2
officialTextEn: If Control of a Battlefield is Contested, there aren’t units controlled by different players there, and the turn is in a Neutral Open State, a Showdown is opened during the next Cleanup. See rule 318. Cleanups for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 345
officialTextEn: As a Showdown begins, the player who applied Contested status to the Battlefield gains Focus.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 346
officialTextEn: When the last item on the chain resolves and the turn returns to an Open State during a Showdown, Focus passes, and the next Player gains both Focus and Priority.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 346.1
officialTextEn: Focus will not pass in this way if the chain opened as a result of a triggered ability being added to the chain, nor if it opened as a result of an Add ability being added to the chain. Example: the Combat Chain opens as a result of triggered abilities being added to the chain, so when the last item on the Combat Chain resolves and the turn returns to an Open State, Focus will not pass.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 347
officialTextEn: During a Showdown, the player with Focus may do one of the following:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 347.1
officialTextEn: Play a Card or Activated Ability that is legally timed.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 347.1.a
officialTextEn: The card or activated ability will start a Chain as normal.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 347.1.b
officialTextEn: When that Chain closes, the next Player in Turn Order gains Focus.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 347.2
officialTextEn: Pass.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 347.2.a
officialTextEn: If all Players have passed once in sequence, the Showdown ends.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 347.2.b
officialTextEn: Otherwise, the next Player in Turn Order gains Focus.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 348
officialTextEn: If all players pass Focus without playing a card or activating an ability, then the Showdown Closes.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 348.1
officialTextEn: If it is a Combat Showdown, proceed with the remaining steps of Combat to resolve the phase. See rule 465. The Steps of Combat for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 348.2
officialTextEn: If it is a Non-Combat Showdown, do the following:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 348.2.a
officialTextEn: If only one player’s Units remain at the Battlefield, and if that player does not already Control the Battlefield, that player establishes Control over the Battlefield. See rule 188. Control for more information on Control. See rule 471.1. for more information on Conquering.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 348.2.a.1
officialTextEn: This results in a Conquer if that player has not yet scored that Battlefield this turn.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 349
officialTextEn: Playing Cards

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 350
officialTextEn: Playing a card is the act of a player utilizing their cards.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 350.1
officialTextEn: A card is Played when it has finished this process in its entirety.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 350.2
officialTextEn: Tokens are not cards, but can still be Played. See rule 179. Tokens for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 351
officialTextEn: Cards have different behaviors when played.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 351.1
officialTextEn: Permanents become Game Objects when Played.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 351.2
officialTextEn: Spells create game effects that are executed, then the card is placed in the trash after resolving.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 352
officialTextEn: Cards have different states during the process of being played.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 352.1
officialTextEn: When initially being played cards are Pending, as Pending Chain Items.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 352.2
officialTextEn: Near the end of the process cards will cease being Pending and become Finalized Chain Items.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 353
officialTextEn: The Process of Play

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 354
officialTextEn: 1. Move the card from its current zone to the Chain.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 354.1
officialTextEn: This Closes the State. See rule 307. States of the Turn for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 354.2
officialTextEn: This item becomes Pending, awaiting the finalization process (steps 2 - 5)

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 354.3
officialTextEn: If another Card Effect or ability is currently resolving, continue resolving it before proceeding with any further steps of this process.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 354.4
officialTextEn: If there are Tasks outstanding or currently being handled, finish those Tasks before continuing this process. See rule 332. for more information on Tasks.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355
officialTextEn: 2. Make relevant choices.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.1
officialTextEn: If the card has an effect that specifies a choice or instructs an action that is not a cost "As I am played," or “As you play me,” those choices or actions are made or performed now.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.1.a
officialTextEn: This includes the choice of whether or not to pay an Optional Additional Cost.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.2
officialTextEn: For Units, choose a valid Location where that Unit will enter upon being Played.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.2.a
officialTextEn: By default, Valid locations include the controller’s Base or a Battlefield the controller controls.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.2.b
officialTextEn: Some Game Effects may grant players permission to play Units to locations that are not normally Valid. Such locations become Valid for the purposes of Playing the Unit.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.3
officialTextEn: For Spells and Abilities with a bulleted list of modes to choose from, make the appropriate choices now.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.4
officialTextEn: For Spells and Abilities that Move one or more Units, choose a valid Location as the Move Destination for each Move that will be performed.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.4.a
officialTextEn: A valid Location for a Move Effect is one other than the Units’ current Location where they are allowed to be present.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.5
officialTextEn: If a card requires you to specifically choose one or more Game Objects, that choice is made now.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.5.a
officialTextEn: This does not include cards that affect one or more Game Objects based on criteria. Example: "Stun a unit at a battlefield" is a Choice. Example: "Kill all gear" is not a Choice.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.5.b
officialTextEn: This does not include making choices for Triggered Abilities of permanents, or Delayed or Reflexive Triggers generated by the item being finalized, even if those abilities trigger when the chain item is played. Example: A unit with a triggered ability that says "When I'm played, kill a unit" does not require you to choose a target as it's played. The target will be chosen when the ability triggers. Example: Targon’s Peak reads “When you conquer here, ready up to 2 runes at the end of this turn.” Readying up to 2 runes at the end of the turn is the effect of a delayed trigger; any choices involved are not made when finalizing the conquer effect but when finalizing the resulting delayed trigger at the end of the turn. See rule 382. Triggered Abilities for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.6
officialTextEn: Targeting

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.7
officialTextEn: When a card Chooses one or more specific Game Objects, Players, or Zones to affect, they are Targeted unless indicated otherwise by the rules in this section. If a card Picks one or more specific Game Objects, Players, or zones, they are not Targeted.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.8
officialTextEn: In order to put a spell or ability on the chain, valid choices must be made for all targets.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.9
officialTextEn: A target is a valid choice if it meets all of the following requirements:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.9.a
officialTextEn: It is a permanent or rune on the board, a finalized spell or ability on the chain, a player or zone, or a game object specified explicitly or implicitly as being in some other zone. e.g., “Kill a unit” targets a unit on the board. e.g., “Recycle a unit from your trash” targets a unit card in your trash.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.9.a.1
officialTextEn: “Unit,” “gear,” and “rune” refer to objects on the Board unless specified otherwise.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.9.a.2
officialTextEn: “Spell” and “ability” refer to finalized objects on the Chain unless specified otherwise.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.9.a.3
officialTextEn: “Facedown card” refers to a card in a Facedown Zone unless specified otherwise.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.9.a.4
officialTextEn: “Legend” refers to a legend in the Legend Zone.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.9.a.5
officialTextEn: “Chosen Champion” and “unit in the Champion Zone” refer to a unit in the Champion Zone unless specified otherwise.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.9.b
officialTextEn: It meets all targeting restrictions. e.g., A unit is a valid target for a spell that refers to a “unit at a battlefield,” “enemy unit,” “unit you control,” or “unit with Might 4 or greater” only if it meets the appropriate criteria. e.g. A unit that reads “I can’t be chosen by enemy spells or abilities.” is not a valid target for any enemy spell or ability, even if it meets other targeting restrictions.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.9.c
officialTextEn: It is not the spell or ability itself. e.g., A spell that says “Counter a spell” cannot target itself. e.g., An ability of a permanent can target that permanent, because abilities and their sources are separate objects.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.10
officialTextEn: A game object, player, or zone mentioned in the text of a spell, activated ability, or triggered ability is a target UNLESS any of the following are true:

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.10.a
officialTextEn: It is in a zone whose information status is not Public. e.g., “Ready a legend” targets a legend, because the Legend Zone is Public. e.g., “Return a unit from your trash to your hand” targets a unit card in your trash, because your trash is Public. e.g., “You may play a unit from your hand, ignoring its costs” does not target a unit card in your hand, because your hand is not a public zone.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.10.a.1
officialTextEn: Public zones are Battlefield Zones, Bases, Trashes, Legend Zones, Champion Zones, and Facedown Zones.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.10.b
officialTextEn: It is included only as part of a targeting restriction for another choice or only as a restriction or permission for a game action. e.g., “Kill a unit at a battlefield” targets a unit, but not a battlefield, because the units are targets and “at a battlefield” is a restriction. e.g., “Kill all units at a battlefield” targets a battlefield, but not any units. e.g., “Play a unit from your hand to a battlefield” doesn’t target a battlefield.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.10.c
officialTextEn: It is included only as part of a cost, trigger condition, or replacement effect. e.g., “As an additional cost to play me, kill a friendly unit” doesn’t target anything. e.g., “When a friendly unit dies, kill a gear” targets a gear, but not a friendly unit. e.g., “When you play me, the next time a friendly unit would die this turn, return it to your hand instead” doesn’t target anything. The replacement effect applies when any friendly unit dies. e.g., “Choose a friendly unit. The next time it would die this turn, return it to your hand instead” targets a friendly unit, because “choose a friendly unit” is not part of the replacement effect.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.10.c.1
officialTextEn: This includes costs within instructions, identified by phrases like “[do X] to [do Y].” The cost within that instruction is “[do X].” e.g., “When I hold, you may kill another friendly unit here to draw 1” does not target anything. e.g., “When you play me, you may spend a buff to move a friendly unit” targets the friendly unit, but not the buff.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.10.d
officialTextEn: It is programmatically selected based on its characteristics rather than chosen by the spell or ability’s controller. e.g., “Kill all units at a battlefield” targets a battlefield, but does not target any units. e.g., “Kill all units at battlefields” doesn’t target anything. e.g., “Kill a unit. Its controller draws 2” targets the unit, but not its controller. e.g., “Recycle all cards in your trash” doesn’t target anything, because it affects all cards and you only have one trash.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.10.d.1
officialTextEn: This exception applies solely to objects for which no choice is ever possible.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.10.d.2
officialTextEn: This exception does not apply to objects that are the only valid choice at the moment a spell or ability is placed on the chain, but which would require a choice under other circumstances. e.g., “Kill a unit at a battlefield” always targets a unit, even if that unit is the only unit currently at a battlefield.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.10.e
officialTextEn: It is part of a set of objects chosen in whole or in part by other players. e.g., “Each player kills a unit they control” does not target. Each player, including the one who played the spell, chooses a unit to kill as the spell or ability resolves.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.10.f
officialTextEn: It is identified in an instruction that a player “must” complete. e.g., “You must recycle one of your runes” doesn’t target anything. You choose from among your runes as the spell or ability resolves. e.g., “Recycle a rune you control” targets a rune. You choose a rune you control as you put the spell or ability on the chain.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.10.g
officialTextEn: It is a legend “you” control. e.g. “Ready your legend.” doesn’t target any legend. If a player controls multiple legends, they choose one as the spell or ability resolves. e.g. “Ready a friendly legend.” targets the friendly legend. e.g. “Exhaust an enemy legend.” targets the enemy legend.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.11
officialTextEn: Some cards identify a group of Targets with Targeting Requirements that must be met by the group as a whole.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.11.a
officialTextEn: As they’re finalized on the chain, such cards can choose any group of valid targets that collectively fulfill the targeting restriction.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.11.b
officialTextEn: If the group of targets no longer collectively fulfill the targeting restriction as the spell or ability resolves, that spell or ability’s controller must choose a legal subset of the original targets that fulfills the targeting requirement for the spell or ability to affect. Example: A player plays Fox-Fire, a spell that says in part “Kill any number of units at a battlefield with total Might 4 or less.” That player chooses four 1 [M] Recruit tokens at a single battlefield. As a Reaction, another player gives two of those Recruits +1 [M], so the Recruits’ Mights are 1, 1, 2, and 2. Then Fox-Fire resolves. The Recruits no longer have total Might 4 or less, so Fox-Fire’s controller must choose a legal subset of the original targets to affect. They could choose to kill the two 2 [M] Recruits, or the two 1 [M] Recruits plus one 2 [M] Recruit. The units they choose are Fox-Fire’s remaining legal targets. They can’t choose to affect units at the same battlefield that weren’t initially chosen as targets. They can, however, choose to affect units that were initially chosen as targets that left the chosen battlefield before Fox-Fire resolved as long as those units are all located at the same battlefield.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.11.b.1
officialTextEn: Any legal subset must include the maximum number of legal targets possible for that subset. Example: A player plays Bellow’s Breath, a spell that reads in part “Deal 1 to up to 3 units at the same location.” They choose 3 units at the same battlefield. In reaction to Bellow’s Breath, the controller of those units plays Flash, moving two of them to base. On resolution of Bellow’s Breath, Bellow’s Breath’s controller cannot choose one unit in base and not the other. They may choose either of the legal subsets; the one unit remaining at the battlefield, or the two units in base.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.12
officialTextEn: If a spell specifies that a player may perform a Game Action on some number of Game Objects, then all choices are considered targeted and chosen independently of the decision to perform the Game Action.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.13
officialTextEn: If a card specifies that a player chooses “any number” or “up to” some number of Game Objects to be affected, they may choose any number of available targets, including zero. If they choose zero, the spell or ability can be played without any targets.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.14
officialTextEn: Splitting

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.14.a
officialTextEn: If a card specifies that an amount of damage may be split among some number of Units, then each Unit chosen is Targeted.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.14.b
officialTextEn: The Targets are chosen when the spell or ability is finalized on the chain.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.14.c
officialTextEn: A number of Targets can only be chosen up to, and not exceeding, the initial amount of damage available when the spell is played. Example: A player playing a spell that instructs them to "Split 5 damage" may only choose up to 5 units, but may choose fewer.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.14.d
officialTextEn: Each Target is valid, and contributes to Targeting Effects individually.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.14.e
officialTextEn: The choice of how much damage is divided across the split is not decided until the resolution of the spell or ability.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.14.f
officialTextEn: Each Target must receive a valid amount of damage.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.14.g
officialTextEn: Valid damage is a positive integer amount, greater than or equal to 1 damage. See rule 418. Deal for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.14.h
officialTextEn: If, at resolution of the spell or effect, there are more Targets than available damage to divide, then the player who controls the effect dealing damage determines which Targets cease being Targets.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.14.h.1
officialTextEn: That player cannot choose to have fewer Targets than they have damage to split when choosing which Targets cease being Targets. Example: A player plays Alpha Strike, which reads in part “Choose a friendly unit. It deals damage equal to its Might split among enemy units at battlefields.” They target their 5 [M] unit and five 1 [M] enemy Recruits at battlefields. In reaction, their opponent plays Feral Strength targeting one of their recruits, and Frigid Touch targeting the 5 [M] unit. When Alpha Strike resolves, they have 3 damage to split, and must choose which targets cease being targets. They can’t choose for 4 of the units to cease being targets so that they can deal 3 to the 3 [M] recruit. They can only choose at most 2 of the targets to cease being targets.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.14.i
officialTextEn: Any costs that were paid, or effects that were triggered as a result of those Game Objects being chosen as Targets remain in effect, paid, or otherwise triggered.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.15
officialTextEn: These choices cannot be changed after this step unless instructed to by a spell or ability. See rule 750. Making New Choices for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.16
officialTextEn: A player may not make choices during this step that will deterministically result in illegal choices or actions later in this process unless they have no choice. Example: A player plays a card which reads “As an additional cost to play this, kill the unit you control with the most Might. Give a friendly unit +[M] equal to the killed unit’s Might this turn. Predict 2.” They cannot choose to target their unit with the highest Might during this step of finalization.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.17
officialTextEn: If a Game Effect has introduced a mandatory requirement on any of these choices, that mandatory requirement must be followed if possible. A mandatory requirement is one that specifies what choice can be made or how that choice is made, but doesn't specifically disallow other game states. Example: Here to Help is a spell that reads in part “You may play a unit from your hand to a battlefield you control.” If its controller decides to play a unit, they must play it to a battlefield they control. Example: Rek’Sai, Swarm Queen is a unit that reads “When I attack, you may reveal the top 2 cards of your Main Deck. You may banish one, then play it. If it is a unit, you may play it here. Recycle the rest.” The “you may play it here,” portion of this ability is not a mandatory requirement, because the player isn’t required to play the unit to that location.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.17.a
officialTextEn: If there are multiple mandatory requirements that do not conflict, players must make a choice that will satisfy those mandatory requirements. Any individual group of such complementary mandatory requirements that contains as many non-contradictory mandatory requirements as possible forms a set. If there are two or more sets of mandatory requirements that are mutually contradictory, choose one of those sets and ignore the rest. Example: Here to Help is played from facedown at Targon’s Peak. Its controller chooses to play a Dune Drake from hand. The other battlefield is Dragon Roost. When finalizing Dune Drake, they choose to pay the [A][A] additional cost from Dragon Roost. There are two competing mandatory requirements here: playing Dune Drake to Targon’s Peak, or playing it to Dragon Roost. Dune Drake’s controller must choose one of those requirements to satisfy, and ignore the rest. Example: If Here to Help were played from hand, and its controller controlled both battlefields, if they paid the [A][A] additional cost, they would have no choice but to play Dune Drake to Dragon Roost as it would satisfy both mandatory requirements.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.17.b
officialTextEn: If there are one or more restrictions on choices being made during this process, those restrictions must be followed. Failure to do so means the card will fail to finalize. Example: Perched Grimwyrm is a unit that reads “Play me only to a battlefield you conquered this turn.” If a player plays Perched Grimwyrm via Here to Help and they haven’t conquered a battlefield this turn, Perched Grimwyrm will fail to finalize. Although Here to Help presents a mandatory requirement, Perched Grimwyrm’s restriction on being played overrides it. Example: Mageseeker Warden is a unit that reads in part “While I'm at a battlefield, opponents can only play units to their base.” If a player attempts to play a Perched Grimwyrm to a battlefield they’ve conquered this turn while their opponent controls a Mageseeker Warden at a battlefield, the Perched Grimwyrm will fail to finalize.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 355.18
officialTextEn: If a spell or ability requires one or more players to make choices that are not outlined in this section, they are made on resolution.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356
officialTextEn: 3. Determine Total Cost.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.1
officialTextEn: Apply base cost modifications in any order.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.1.a
officialTextEn: If an ability or instruction allows you to play a card “for [Cost]”, replace the card’s Base Costs with [Cost].

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.1.b
officialTextEn: If an ability or instruction allows you to "ignore" one or more of a card's costs, set the appropriate Base Cost(s) of the card to zero.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.1.b.1
officialTextEn: If a card allows a player to play a card "ignoring its cost," its base Energy cost and base Power cost are set to zero.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.1.b.2
officialTextEn: If a card instructs a player to play a card "ignoring its Energy cost" or "ignoring its Power cost," only the appropriate cost is set to zero, and the remaining cost still applies.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.1.b.3
officialTextEn: Further additional costs and/or cost increases applied in subsequent steps may raise the card's Total Cost above zero. Example: Legion Rearguard is a Fury unit that costs 2 Energy and 0 Power and has Accelerate. A player plays Legion Rearguard and is instructed to ignore its costs, but chooses to pay the Accelerate cost. They ignore Legion Rearguard's Base Cost of 2 Energy, but the optional additional cost of 1 Energy and 1 Fury Power is added to its Total Cost and must be paid.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.1.c
officialTextEn: Effects that refer to the Base Cost of the card refer to the Printed or Copied Base Cost of said card, and not the modified Base Cost that is used when determining the total cost of the card.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.2
officialTextEn: Apply additional costs in any order.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.2.a
officialTextEn: Mandatory Additional Costs

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.2.a.1
officialTextEn: Some Additional Costs specified by Passive Abilities on the card being played or another card are Mandatory, and must be paid to complete playing the card. They use the phrase "as an additional cost" and don't include the word "may." Example: A unit has the passive ability "As an additional cost to play me, kill a friendly unit." To play that unit, a player must kill a friendly unit. See rule 363. Passive Abilities for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.2.a.2
officialTextEn: The cost imposed by the Deflect keyword is a Mandatory Additional Cost. See rule 809. Deflect for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.2.b
officialTextEn: Optional Additional Costs

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.2.b.1
officialTextEn: Some Optional Costs specified by Passive Abilities on the card being played or another card are Non-Mandatory, and must be paid only if the player made the choice to pay them in step 2. They use the phrase "as an additional cost" and the word "may." Example: A unit has the ability "As you play me, you may discard 1 as an additional cost. If you do, reduce my cost by [2]." While playing the unit, its controller declares their intention to pay the additional cost in step 2, applies that additional cost in rule 356.2, applies the discount granted by paying that cost in rule 356.4, and discards a card to pay that additional cost in rule 357.2. See rule 363. Passive Abilities for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.3
officialTextEn: Apply cost increases.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.4
officialTextEn: Apply discounts.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.4.a
officialTextEn: Discounts may be applied by the card being played or by any other card or effect.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.4.b
officialTextEn: Discounts may say that cards "cost [amount] less" or that one or more of their costs are "reduced by [amount]."

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.4.c
officialTextEn: Discounts that only apply to a component of the cost will be applied when that component is added to the cost of the spell and before any other discounts. Example: Ezreal, Prodigy reads “optional additional costs you pay cost [1] or [A] less.” When playing a Frigid Touch and choosing to pay the additional cost in step 2, as soon as the additional cost is added to the cost of the spell, Ezreal, Prodigy’s discount is applied to it.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.4.c.1
officialTextEn: Discounts that apply to a given component of a spell’s cost may be applied in any order to that component, and apply only to that component.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.4.c.2
officialTextEn: Discounts that apply to a given component of a spell’s cost cannot reduce that component to less than 0.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.4.d
officialTextEn: Discounts that apply to the total cost of a spell and not any one component of the cost must be applied after any discount that applies only to a component of the cost.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.4.d.1
officialTextEn: These discounts may be applied in any order as long as they are applied after component discounts.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.4.e
officialTextEn: If a discount applies a minimum cost, that minimum applies only to that discount. Example: Eager Apprentice says "While I'm at a battlefield, the Energy costs for spells you play is reduced by [1], to a minimum of [1]." A player who controls Eager Apprentice and a unit with 7 Might plays Sky Splitter, a spell that costs 8 Energy and says "This spell's Energy cost is reduced by the highest Might among units you control." That player can choose to apply Eager Apprentice's discount first, reducing Sky Splitter's Energy cost to 7, then apply Sky Splitter's discount, reducing its Energy cost to 0. If they applied these discounts in the other order, Sky Splitter's Energy cost would be 1.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.4.f
officialTextEn: Discounts can reduce additional costs, including to 0.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.4.f.1
officialTextEn: An optional additional cost was "paid" if the player made the decision to pay it. It doesn't matter how much the player actually paid. Example: Clockwork Keeper is a unit that costs 2 Energy and 0 Power and says "As you play me, you may pay [C] as an additional cost. If you do, draw 1." A player controls a card that says "Units you play cost [A] less." That player plays Clockwork Keeper and chooses to pay the optional additional cost of [C]. They will draw a card, even though the optional additional cost was reduced to 0.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.4.g
officialTextEn: If a discount applies a variable cost reduction to the card, that value is checked now. Example: Rhasa, the Sunderer reads “I cost [1] less for each card in your trash.” The value of this discount depends on the number of cards in the trash. That value is checked during this step when the discount is applied to Rhasa’s cost. If the number of cards in his controller’s trash changes at a later point in the finalization process, that will not affect the value checked during this step or the total cost calculated in this step.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.5
officialTextEn: Apply modifications to the total cost in any order.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.5.a
officialTextEn: If an effect allows a player to play a card ignoring “any and all costs,” set the total cost to [0], including any non-standard costs.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.6
officialTextEn: Energy and Power costs can't be reduced below 0.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 356.7
officialTextEn: Costs may be Energy costs, Power costs, or non-standard costs. Example: A card reads "As an additional cost to play me, kill a friendly unit." Killing a friendly unit is an additional cost to play that card.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 357
officialTextEn: 4. Pay the card's costs.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 357.1
officialTextEn: In total, pay the combined Energy cost (if any) and Power cost (if any).

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 357.1.a
officialTextEn: During this step, the card's controller can use activated abilities with the Reaction tag that Add resources to add Energy and Power to pay the card's costs. See rule 165. Rune Pools and rule 430. Add for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 357.2
officialTextEn: In addition, pay any non-standard Cost summed in step 3 in any order. Example: A card reads in part “As an additional cost to play me, kill a friendly unit and discard a unit.” When paying the costs for that card, its controller can pay those two costs in any order; they can kill a friendly unit first and then discard a unit, or they can discard a unit and then kill a friendly unit.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 357.2.a
officialTextEn: Costs that are replaced with other events by replacement effects are still considered paid. Example: A player plays Cruel Patron, which says "As an additional cost to play me, kill a friendly unit." They also control Zhonya’s Hourglass, which says “If a friendly unit would die, kill this instead. Heal that unit, exhaust it, and recall it.” They choose to kill a friendly unit during step 3, but as they pay the cost in step 4, Zhonya’s Hourglass replaces that unit’s death. The cost is considered paid, and the player can continue playing Cruel Patron.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 357.3
officialTextEn: A player may not pay costs during this step that will deterministically result in illegal choices or actions later in this process unless they have no choice. Example: A player plays a card which reads “as an additional cost to play this, you may kill a friendly unit. Give a friendly unit +2 [M] this turn. If you paid the cost, give that unit +7 [M] this turn instead” If they chose to pay the cost, they must choose to kill a unit other than the targeted unit unless they have no choice.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 358
officialTextEn: 5. Check legality.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 358.1
officialTextEn: Check that the card made appropriate choices. Example: If the card chose targets, ensure that the targets are legal. Example: If the card made choices that had restrictions or requirements, ensure that restrictions were followed and that the requirements were met as appropriate. See rule 355. Make Relevant Choices for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 358.2
officialTextEn: Check that all costs were paid.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 358.3
officialTextEn: Check that the outcome of the effect of this card being played would not create an illegal state. Example: Check that a spell's execution does not create a state where a Battlefield has Units controlled by 3 different players. Example: Check that a permanent is not played to a base other than that of its controller.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 358.3.a
officialTextEn: If a Game Effect prevents the performance of a game action, that effect doesn’t prevent cards and abilities that instruct a player to perform that game action from being played or finalized. Example: Flash is a spell that reads in part “Move up to 2 friendly units to base.” Vilemaw’s Lair is a battlefield that reads “Units can’t move from here to base.” Flash is legal to play choosing a unit at Vilemaw’s Lair; on resolution of the spell, the move instruction will be negated.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 358.3.b
officialTextEn: This check only extends to the resolution of the current card. Any Reflexive Triggers, cards played, or abilities triggered as a result of the execution must be evaluated on their own merits as they finalize.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 358.4
officialTextEn: Check that the card has the appropriate permissions to be played at this timing. Example: If the state is Showdown Closed and the card was the one that Closed the state, ensure that it has [Action] or [Reaction]. Example: If the state is Closed and the card wasn’t the one that Closed the state, ensure that it has [Reaction].

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 358.5
officialTextEn: If any of the above checks fail, the actions taken in this process are undone, any effects that those actions caused to occur are treated as having never happened, and the action is cancelled.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359
officialTextEn: 6. Finish finalizing this card and proceed with the card's category of Play.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.1
officialTextEn: This card is no longer Pending.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.2
officialTextEn: A Permanent leaves the Chain and becomes a Game Object.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.2.a
officialTextEn: Any passive abilities become active.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.2.b
officialTextEn: Execute all rules text on the card, from top to bottom.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.2.c
officialTextEn: If it is a Unit, it enters the Board exhausted at the Location that was chosen.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.2.d
officialTextEn: If it is a Non-Unit Gear, it enters the Board Ready at the player's Base.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3
officialTextEn: A Spell lingers on the Chain.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.a
officialTextEn: This card becomes a Finalized Chain Item.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.b
officialTextEn: If there are other Pending Items on the Chain, then the controller of those Pending Items completes Steps 2 through 5 of Playing Cards for those items before continuing. See rule 327. Chains for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.c
officialTextEn: Other players have an opportunity to play Reactions before the resolution of spells. See rule 327. Chains for more information.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.d
officialTextEn: Otherwise, execute the game effect of the spell, from top to bottom of the rules text of the card and then place the card in the Trash of the owning player.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.e
officialTextEn: Handling illegal and impossible instructions

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.e.1
officialTextEn: The spell resolves even if some or all of its targets are illegal.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.e.2
officialTextEn: A target is illegal as the spell resolves if it no longer meets the targeting requirements of the spell, or if it has changed Zones to or from a Non-Board Zone.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.e.2.a
officialTextEn: This includes targeting restrictions that are applied to the spell by game effects other than the spell’s instructions themselves. Example: Temporal Breach is a spell that reads in part “Banish a unit, then its owner plays it to the same location, ignoring its cost.” By default, the only targeting restrictions on the spell are that the target is a unit, and that the unit is able to be chosen by the spell. However, if Temporal Breach is played from facedown, it gains the restriction that it must choose from among game objects at the battlefield it was played from. If the unit it chooses moves to a different location, that unit will be an illegal target on resolution of Temporal Breach.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.e.3
officialTextEn: If a target ceases to meet the targeting requirements while the spell is on the chain, then meets them again, it's a legal target. Example: A spell targets "a unit at a battlefield." A player reacts with a spell that moves the unit to base, then another player reacts with a spell that moves it back to that battlefield, then the original spell resolves. The unit is a legal target.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.e.4
officialTextEn: If a target changes Zones to or from a Non-Board Zone and then returns to its original zone, it is no longer a legal target, because it's not treated as the same object. Examples: An enemy unit at a battlefield is no longer a legal target if it is no longer an enemy, no longer a unit, or no longer at a battlefield. A unit with 3 or less Might is no longer a legal target if it is no longer a unit or if its Might is greater than 3. Something that's exhausted is no longer a legal target if it is no longer exhausted. (It can't stop being "something.")

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.e.5
officialTextEn: If any of the spell's targets are no longer legal, those game objects, players, or zones are unaffected by the spell as it resolves. Any instructions related to an illegal target can’t be followed. Example: A player plays Void Seeker, a spell that says "Deal 4 to a unit at a battlefield. Draw 1." The unit's controller uses a Reaction to move the unit to their base. Since the unit is no longer a legal target, it is not dealt any damage. Void Seeker's controller still draws 1. Example: A player plays Bellow’s Breath targeting a unit in combat that reads in part “I can’t be chosen by enemy spells and abilities unless I’m in combat.” In reaction, that unit’s controller plays Flash, moving the unit to their base. The unit is no longer in combat, so it is no longer a legal target for Bellow’s Breath. The unit will be unaffected by Bellow’s Breath as it resolves. Example: A player plays Hidden Blade from the facedown zone at a battlefield, targeting an enemy unit. In reaction to Hidden Blade, their opponent plays Tideturner from facedown at another battlefield, choosing to swap locations with the unit Hidden Blade targeted. When Hidden Blade resolves, the chosen unit is no longer at the appropriate battlefield, so any instructions related to that unit are ignored.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.e.6
officialTextEn: Instructions that can't be followed because of illegal targets, or because they reference information that is unavailable, are considered Ignored. Instructions that can’t be followed for any other reason are Negated. Example: A player plays Ride the Wind choosing to move their unit at Vilemaw’s Lair to base. Base is a legal move destination for Ride the Wind, but on resolution of Ride the Wind’s effect, the move instruction will be negated because Vilemaw’s restriction makes the instruction impossible. Example: A player plays Hidden Blade targeting a unit at a battlefield. In reaction to Hidden Blade, the unit’s controller plays Flash, moving it to base. Hidden Blade’s instruction “Kill a unit.” will be ignored on resolution of the spell.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.e.7
officialTextEn: If all of an instruction's Targets become Invalid or Unavailable by the time the spell begins resolving, that instruction will not execute.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.e.8
officialTextEn: If an instruction has more than one Target and fewer than all of the Targets become Invalid or Unavailable by the time the spell begins resolving, the instruction will execute, with only the Targets available and valid being operated on. Example: Singularity reads “deal 6 to each of up to two units.” The instruction will execute even if one of those units is made unavailable before the spell begins.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.e.9
officialTextEn: The process for a card's choice becoming Invalid or Unavailable is referred to as Mistargeting. Example: A spell has the instruction "Deal 2 to a unit at a battlefield." Before that instruction can execute, the chosen unit is moved to its base. The instruction will not be executed, because it specifies that the unit it chooses must be at a Battlefield, and by the time it attempted to execute, the unit was no longer valid as a choice.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.e.9.a
officialTextEn: If another spell or ability attempts to reference the number of game objects, players, or zones that a Finalized Chain Item targets, it will include any mistargeted choices in the zone specified implicitly or explicitly by the instruction that targeted them, but not any targets that have changed to or from a non-board zone. Example: When a player moves their Volibear, Furious to an occupied enemy battlefield and combat initiates, Volibear’s attack trigger goes on the chain targeting three of the units at that battlefield. In reaction, the defending player plays Flash moving two of the three units back. That player cannot then target the attack trigger with Repulse, which reads “Choose a friendly unit at a battlefield. Counter an enemy spell or ability that chooses it and no other friendly unit.” If the defending player instead played Heedless Resurrection twice, killing the two units, Repulse can legally target the attack trigger, because two of the targets have changed to a non-board zone.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.e.10
officialTextEn: It is possible for none of a spell's instructions to be executed as it resolves, due to all of them requiring targets to act on and all of those targets becoming Invalid or Unavailable. In this case, the spell has no effect but is still considered played. Example: A player plays a spell that reads "Deal 2 to a unit at a battlefield" with no other instructions, and chooses an enemy unit at a battlefield. They also control a unit with the ability "When you play a spell, give me +1 [M] this turn." Before the spell resolves, the chosen unit is moved to its base. The spell resolves and its only instruction cannot be executed, but the unit's ability still triggers as the spell resolves and gives it +1 [M].

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.e.11
officialTextEn: Instructions that can be partially followed are followed as much as possible and negated otherwise. Example: A player plays a spell that says "Discard 2, then draw 2." If their hand is empty, the instruction to discard 2 will be negated. They'll still draw 2. If they had 1 card in hand, they would discard it and draw 2.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.e.12
officialTextEn: If the spell checks information about a target that is no longer legal or a card or permanent whose location, zone, or status has changed such that that information is no longer available, that check returns "null" and all instructions based on it are Ignored. Examples: A unit that is no longer on the board is treated as having null Might, null cost, etc. A unit that is no longer on the board has no location, is neither exhausted nor readied, etc. Baited Hook says "[1][C], [E]: Kill a friendly unit. Look at the top 5 cards of your Main Deck. You may banish a unit from among them that has Might up to 1 more than the killed unit and play it, ignoring its cost. Then recycle the rest." While Baited Hook’s ability is on the chain, an opponent reacts with a spell that returns the friendly unit to its owner's hand. Because the friendly unit is no longer a legal target, it can't be killed and its Might is treated as null. Baited Hook’s controller looks at the top 5 cards of their Main Deck, but can’t choose any unit from among them. Strike Down reads “Choose an equipped friendly unit. It deals damage equal to its Might to an enemy unit. Then detach an Equipment from it.” While Strike Down is on the chain targeting a unit with only one Equipment attached to it, that unit has its Equipment detached via Angle Shot. When Strike Down goes to resolve, the targeted unit is no longer legal, so the unit’s Might will return as “null” and the instructions related to it are ignored.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.e.12.a
officialTextEn: If the spell checks information about a target that is legal or a card or permanent whose location, zone, or status has not changed such that information is no longer available, that information is accessible.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.e.13
officialTextEn: A spell or ability that moves something to a different zone as a cost or effect can "look back" at its characteristics before it changes zones.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.e.14
officialTextEn: Some instructions may reference Game Objects affected by, or Game Actions performed in, other instructions in a card. The referenced and referencing instructions are called “linked instructions.” Example: Hidden Blade reads “Kill a unit at a battlefield. Its controller draws 2.” The “its” in the second instruction references the unit in the first, so the two instructions of the spell are linked.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.e.14.a
officialTextEn: In order for a later linked instruction to execute, its earlier linked instruction must have executed or been negated. If the earlier linked instruction is Ignored, the later linked instruction will also be Ignored. If any individual target of an earlier linked instruction is ignored, it will also be ignored by any later linked instruction. Example: Hidden Blade reads “Kill a unit at a battlefield. Its controller draws 2.” If the chosen unit changes zones or moves to base in reaction to Hidden Blade, the spell will mistarget and the first instruction will be ignored. If the first instruction is ignored, the second instruction will not execute and the unit’s controller will not draw 2.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.e.14.b
officialTextEn: If the Game Action performed in an earlier linked instruction is Negated, this will not affect the later linked instruction, unless the later linked instruction directly references the Game Action being performed. An instruction is Negated if the event its execution generates is replaced or skipped, or if the game action can’t be performed because of a reason other than it being Ignored. Example: Hidden Blade reads “Kill a unit at a battlefield. Its controller draws 2.” This effect is split into two instructions: killing the unit and the targeted unit’s controller drawing 2. The later linked instruction doesn’t reference an action directly, so it will execute even if the kill action of the earlier linked action is negated. Example: Deathgrip reads “Kill a friendly unit. If you do, give +[M] equal to its Might to another friendly unit this turn.” If the friendly unit in question is not killed by Deathgrip because its death is replaced with another event, the later linked instruction will not execute because “if you do” directly references the game action. Example: Ride the Wind is a spell that reads in part “Move a friendly unit and ready it.” Vilemaw’s Lair is a battlefield that reads “Units can’t move from here to base.” If Ride the Wind is played on a unit at Vilemaw’s Lair choosing the base as its destination, the move instruction will be negated on resolution by the passive ability of Vilemaw’s Lair, but the ready instruction will still execute.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.e.14.c
officialTextEn: Referencing a game action in this way only refers to the game action being performed and the object or player it was performed on, not the circumstances of its performance. Example: A spell reads “Deal 3 to an enemy unit at a battlefield. If you do, heal units you control at the same location as that unit.” If some but not all of that damage is prevented, the later linked instruction will still execute. Example: A spell reads “Banish an enemy unit at a battlefield, then play it to any battlefield. Then if you do, do this: stun all enemy units there.” A player plays it targeting a unit that has a passive replacement effect that reads “I enter in base.” The replacement effect causes the unit to enter in base, but this does not prevent the reflexive trigger of the spell from being placed on the chain. All that matters is that the unit was played.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.e.15
officialTextEn: A spell or ability that leaves the chain during the process of its resolution will cease further execution of its instructions. This immediately causes the spell or ability to finish resolving.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.e.16
officialTextEn: If a Delayed Ability’s duration has ended before it was generated, the Delayed Ability is not generated and any instructions related to it are ignored. Example: Targon’s Peak is a battlefield that reads in part “When you conquer here, ready up to 2 runes at the end of this turn.” If Targon’s Peak is conquered during the Ending Phase after the beginning of the ending step, such as via an effect like Thrill of the Hunt, the delayed trigger will not be generated. Example: Hostile Takeover is a spell that reads “Take control of an enemy unit at a battlefield. Ready it.” and “Lose control of that unit and recall it at end of turn.” If Hostile Takeover is played during the Ending Phase, its delayed triggered ability will not trigger. “At end of turn” and “at the end of this turn” are synonymous, so it will not trigger again. Example: Akshan, Mischievous reads in part “When you play me, if you paid the additional cost, move an enemy gear to your base. You control it until I leave the board. If it's an Equipment, attach it to me.” If Akshan leaves the board in reaction to his play effect, the delayed passive ability “You control it until I leave the board,” will not be generated. You will not gain control of the targeted gear even for a moment.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.f
officialTextEn: Referents

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.f.1
officialTextEn: Some information used by abilities is referenced from the source of those abilities, or from one or more targets of a spell or ability. This can usually be recognized by the presence of words like “here,” “my,” or “its.”

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.f.2
officialTextEn: Information referenced in an instruction in this way will be checked on execution of the instruction, unless specified otherwise by the effect. Examples: A player moves Yasuo, Remorseful to an occupied enemy battlefield and initiates combat there. In reaction to the Yasuo, Remorseful attack trigger, their opponent plays Fight or Flight from facedown targeting Yasuo, moving him back to base. When the attack trigger resolves, “here” is no longer the battlefield where combat is ongoing and the attack trigger mistargets. In reaction to a Yasuo, Remorseful attack trigger, an opponent plays Stupefy targeting Yasuo. When Yasuo’s attack trigger resolves, it will deal damage equal to his current Might of 5.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.f.2.a
officialTextEn: When a referent checks information on execution of the instruction related to a target, and that target isn’t legal, that referent will return “null” and all instructions related to it will be ignored.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.f.3
officialTextEn: Some information used by triggered abilities is referenced from the trigger condition of the ability. This information is checked when the trigger condition is fulfilled. Example: Lillia, Fae Fawn reads “when I move from a location, play a 3 [M] Sprite token with Temporary there.” If Lillia moves to a battlefield, her triggered ability will be placed on the chain and it will note the location she moved from when it does so. If she moves to a non-board zone in reaction to the triggered ability on the chain, it will not affect where the Sprite token will be played when the triggered ability resolves.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.f.3.a
officialTextEn: In the case of a delayed triggered ability, the information is referenced when the triggered ability is created unless specified otherwise.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.f.3.b
officialTextEn: In the case of a linked ability that references information from a linked triggered ability, that information may be referenced from the trigger condition of the linked triggered ability if specified. Example: Iascylla reads “When I hold, at the start of your next Main Phase, you may move an enemy unit to this battlefield.” The “this battlefield” in her delayed triggered ability refers to the battlefield she held, and so will be referenced from the trigger condition, when the triggered ability is generated.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 359.3.f.4
officialTextEn: Some information used by the effect of a triggered ability is referenced from the triggered ability itself, such as “enemy” and “friendly” status. This information is checked on execution of the referencing instruction. Example: Yasuo, Remorseful reads “when I attack, deal damage equal to my Might to an enemy unit here.” Yasuo moves to an occupied enemy battlefield and his attack trigger goes on the chain. In reaction to the attack trigger, the defending player plays a hidden Hostile Takeover and gains control of Yasuo. The triggered ability is unaffected by Yasuo changing controllers, and “enemy” is in reference to the triggered ability itself, so it will resolve with no issue. Example: In reaction to the same Yasuo, Remorseful trigger, say the defending player had instead played a spell that reads “[Reaction]. Gain control of a triggered ability. You may make new choices for it.” They chose the attack trigger. When Yasuo’s attack trigger resolves, if they didn’t make new choices for the trigger, the controller of the triggered ability will no longer be an enemy to the targeted unit, so the triggered ability will mistarget and do nothing. If they instead chose Yasuo with the attack trigger, he would be an enemy unit to the triggered ability and so it would deal damage equal to his Might to himself.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 360
officialTextEn: Abilities

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 361
officialTextEn: An Ability is the structured rules and capabilities of Game Objects or Spells.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 361.1
officialTextEn: An Ability has multiple structures. Passive Abilities Replacement Effects Activated Abilities Triggered Abilities Delayed Abilities

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 362
officialTextEn: A card can have more than one Ability and more than one type of Ability.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 363
officialTextEn: Passive Abilities

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 364
officialTextEn: Conditions, rules, constraints, or statements that affect the course of regular play.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 364.1
officialTextEn: These abilities have a wide variety of formats to recognize. Example: "I get +1 [M] while you have 2 or more cards in your hand." Example: "Friendly Yordles at my battlefield have [Shield]."

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 364.2
officialTextEn: They can be recognized by being statements of fact.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 364.3
officialTextEn: Passive Abilities can be conditional.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 364.3.a
officialTextEn: Conditional Passive Abilities can be recognized by the occurrence of "if" or "while" as part of the statement of the ability. Example: "While I'm attacking or defending alone, I have +2 [M]." Example: "If an opponent controls a battlefield, I enter ready."

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 365
officialTextEn: Presence on Permanents

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 365.1
officialTextEn: Passive Abilities of Permanents are typically only active while on the Board.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 366
officialTextEn: Presence on Card outside of the Board

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 366.1
officialTextEn: Passive Abilities of cards in zones that are outside of the Board will self-describe their context. Example: The passive ability "Play me only during an opponent's turn." applies in any zone from which that card can be played. Example: Undying Legion has a passive ability that reads “[Legion][>] You may play me from your trash for [3][C].” That passive ability only applies when Undying Legion is in the trash.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 366.2
officialTextEn: Passive Abilities can alter the costs of cards as they are played.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 366.2.a
officialTextEn: These apply at all times in any zone from which the card with the ability can be played.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 367
officialTextEn: Replacement Effects

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 368
officialTextEn: An ability that alters the application of another game effect or game rule.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 368.1
officialTextEn: Passive Abilities can be Replacement Effects.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 369
officialTextEn: Replacement Effects intercede during the execution of a Game Effect and alter its execution.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 369.1
officialTextEn: A Replacement Effect can usually be identified by the presence of the terms “as,” “would,” or "instead." Example: Zhonya's Hourglass reads "The next time a friendly unit would die, kill this instead. Heal that unit, exhaust it, and recall it." This is a replacement effect that alters the execution of any Game Effect that would kill a friendly unit. Example: Undertitan is a unit that reads in part “As I’m revealed from your deck, [Add] [2].” This is a replacement effect that alters the execution of any Game Effect that reveals Undertitan from your deck.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 369.2
officialTextEn: Some Game Actions are themselves Replacement Effects. Example: Burning Out is a replacement effect. Example: Preventing Damage is a replacement effect.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 369.3
officialTextEn: Replacement Effects that apply to a unit as it enters the Board can be identified by describing how the unit enters, or by describing a game action that occurs “as” a unit enters. Example: Master Yi, Honed reads “I enter ready.” This applies a replacement effect to the way that units normally enter. The event of him entering exhausted is replaced by one where he enters ready. Example: Baron Nashor reads “As you play me, add the Baron Pit battlefield token to the board if it's not there already. If you do, I enter there.” The last sentence of his ability is a replacement effect that replaces the event of him entering at his original play location with him entering at the Baron Pit if it was created.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 370
officialTextEn: A Replacement Effect can alter the typical flow of play, including other cards' executions.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 370.1
officialTextEn: Replacement Effects apply to any event or instruction that qualifies for their application. A Replacement Effect will specify the circumstances by which an event or instruction will qualify to be replaced.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 370.1.a
officialTextEn: An event is the singular moment that results from a Game Action being performed or from a Game Object changing state. Example: The moment that results from a unit being killed is an event that can be referenced by game effects, or even skipped entirely. Example: The moment that results from a unit becoming Mighty is an event that can be referenced by game effects, or even skipped entirely.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 370.1.a.1
officialTextEn: Modifying or replacing an event is the same as modifying or replacing that Game Action or change in state that generated that event. Example: Zhonya’s Hourglass reads in part “If a friendly unit would die, kill this instead. Heal that unit, exhaust it, and recall it.” A unit’s death being replaced by Zhonya’s Hourglass is the same as the kill action that caused that death not occurring. Example: A card reads in part “The next time an enemy unit would become Mighty this turn, banish it instead. Its controller plays a 3 [M] Mech unit token to its location.” A unit becoming Mighty being replaced by this effect means the unit never became Mighty—no effects that trigger on units becoming Mighty will trigger.

title: Riftbound Core Rules · 370.1.a.2
officialTextEn: An event can occur simultaneously with other events only when those events are all the result of the same Game Action or change in state occurring. Example: A spell reads in part “Kill up to two units at battlefields.” When that spell resolves, the units targeted are killed simultaneously because their deaths result from the same game action.
